docs.html:
Chapters 1 to 5 of Intensive Japanese 1 teach you to say what something is, where it is, how many there are, when it happens, and how long it takes. Each chapter below gives the patterns in plain words, the vocabulary worth locking in, the mix-ups to watch for, and a few questions to test yourself. Answers are at the end.

The five chapters at a glance

The chapters build on each other: one basic sentence first, then where things are, then how many, then when, then how long.

ChapterTopicMain patternsSample sentence
1Copula sentences (X is Y)A wa B desu, no / to / ka / mo, kore / sore / are, question wordsWatashi wa gakusei desu. (I am a student.)
2Existence and locationLocation ni A ga arimasu / imasu, A wa Location ni arimasu / imasu, position wordsHeya ni neko ga imasu. (There is a cat in the room.)
3Counting, prices, phone numbersNumbers up to 100 million, ikura desu ka, countersKippu wa hyaku hachijuu en desu. (The ticket is 180 yen.)
4Time expressionsTime desu, kara, made, choudo, goro, itsuミーティングは さんじです。 (Mi-tingu wa sanji desu.) The meeting is at 3 o'clock.
5Span of timeSpan desu, ni for frequency, gurai, mae / sugi, de for transport, kakarimasuバスで きゅうふん かかります。 (Basu de kyuufun kakarimasu.) It takes 9 minutes by bus.

The writing changes as you go. Chapters 1 to 3 are all in romaji. Hiragana starts in Chapter 4, katakana words carry a romaji guide until Chapter 7, and kanji begins in Chapter 8.

Every chapter follows the same loop: goi (vocabulary), bunkei (sentence patterns), reibun (sample sentences), then renshuu (exercises). The exercises come in six sets: choosing the right grammar, rearranging words, filling in a passage, reading comprehension, question and answer, and translating English into Japanese.

Before Chapter 1: sounds and greetings

Japanese is spelled the way it sounds, but a few special sounds change a word if you skip them.

Special sounds

  • Double consonant: hold a short pause before the second consonant, as in hakkiri, hoppeta, motta, katta.
  • Long vowels: stretch the vowel for about two beats, as in arigatou, koukou, sensei, douzo. Length matters, so drill pairs like toki, touki and tokki.
  • Contracted sounds: a small ya, yu or yo blends into the sound before it in one beat, as in gyuunyuu, toukyou, myouji.
  • Weak i and u: sometimes they are almost silent, as in desu, kikimasu, ryuugakusei, wakatteimasu.
  • N before b, m or p sounds like m: shinbun, sanma, kanpai.
  • The ng sound: tenki sounds like tengki and arigatou like aringatou.

Chapter 1: Copula sentences (X is Y)

Chapter 1 is built on one sentence, A wa B desu, and everything else is a small tweak to it.

The core pattern

Wa marks what you are talking about, desu closes the sentence like "is, am, are", and ka at the end turns it into a question.

PatternMeaningExample
A wa B desuA is BWatashi wa gakusei desu. (I am a student.)
A wa B dewa arimasen / ja arimasenA is not BWatashi wa nihonjin dewa arimasen. (I am not Japanese.)
A wa B desu kaIs A B?Sensei wa nihonjin desu ka. (Is the teacher Japanese?)
A no BA's B, B of AWatashi no ofisu (my office), ADZ no shachou (the president of ADZ)
A to BA and Bsensei to gakusei (teacher and student)
A ka BA or Botoko ka onna (male or female)
C mo B desuC is also BHaha mo kaishain desu. (My mother is also an employee.)
A mo B desu kaIs A also B?Ana san mo gakusei desu ka. (Is Ana also a student?)

Answering yes/no questions

You want to saySayIt means
YesHai, (Kim san wa) kenshuusei desu.Yes, (Kim is) a trainee.
NoIie, (Kim san wa) kenshuusei ja arimasen.No, (Kim is) not a trainee.
Yes, that's rightHai, sou desu.Yes, that's correct.
No, that's wrongIie, chigaimasu.No, that's incorrect, it's different.
No, and here is the right answerIie, Ana san wa kaishain desu.No, Ana is an employee.

In conversation you can drop the (A wa) part when it is obvious. When you follow a no with the correct answer, the positive desu comes back.

This, that, which (ko, so, a, do)

Before a nounThingPlaceDirection
ko (near me)konokorekokokochira
so (near you)sonosoresokosochira
a (far from both)anoareasokoachira
do (which?)donodoredokodochira
  • Kono, sono, ano always need a noun after them: kono hon (this book).
  • Kore, sore, are stand alone and point to things: Kore wa watashi no no-to desu. (This is my notebook.)
  • Koko, soko, asoko are places: Koko wa watashi no heya desu. (Here is my room.)
  • Kochira, sochira, achira are directions, and a more formal way to say a place. Kochira is also how you introduce a person: Kochira wa Kimura san desu. (This is Mr. Kimura.)

WordMeaningExample

nannowhat kind ofAre wa nanno kaisha desu ka. (What kind of company is that?)
dokowhereGakkou wa doko desu ka. (Where is your school?)
dochirawhich wayChuushajou wa dochira desu ka. (Which way is the parking lot?)
dorewhich oneAna san no kuruma wa dore desu ka. (Which is Ana's car?)
dono + nounwhich (noun)Eigo no hon wa dono hon desu ka. (Which is the English book?)

A question word simply takes the place of the answer, and the sentence ends in desu ka.

Anata (you) is not normally used with someone you do not know well or with a superior. Use the person's name plus san instead.

Watch out

  • Mo turns into wa in a no answer: Ana san mo gakusei desu ka. Iie, Ana san wa gakusei ja arimasen.
  • Dewa arimasen and ja arimasen mean the same thing. Ja is the shorter, more casual form.
  • Kono, sono, ano need a noun right after them. Kore, sore, are do not.
  • A no B covers a lot: belonging (watashi no ofisu), role (ADZ no shachou) and description (nihongo no gakusei, a Japanese language student).
  • Nan becomes nani when a marker follows it, so you will see nani ga but nan desu ka.

Chapter 2: Existence and location (is there, where is)

Chapter 2 gives you two verbs for being somewhere, arimasu for things and imasu for people and animals, and two sentence shapes to use them in.

Pick the verb

FormNon-living thingsPeople and animals
is, there isarimasuimasu
is not, there is notarimasenimasen
questionarimasu kaimasu ka

Two shapes, two jobs

ShapeUse it toExample
A wa Location ni arimasu / imasusay where something you already know about isGinkou wa asoko ni arimasu. (The bank is over there.) Ana san wa nihon ni imasu. (Ana is in Japan.)
Location ni A ga arimasu / imasusay that something exists in a placeHeya ni terebi ga arimasu. (There is a TV in the room.) Heya ni neko ga imasu. (There is a cat in the room.)

The first shape answers "where is it?". The second answers "what is there?" or "is there one?".

  • Negatives swap in arimasen or imasen: Ginkou wa asoko ni arimasen. (The bank is not over there.)
  • Questions add ka: Anata no ofisu wa Shinjuku ni arimasu ka. (Is your office in Shinjuku?) Kaisha ni chuushajou ga arimasu ka. (Is there a parking lot in your company?)
  • In the ga shape, a negative can add wa after ni for emphasis: Heya ni (wa) isu ga arimasen. (There are no chairs in the room.)

Position words

To say exactly where, name the thing first, then no, then the position word: tsukue no ue (on top of the desk), kaban no naka (inside the bag), eki no mae (in front of the station).

KanaRomajiEnglish
うえueon top, above
したshitaunder, below
まえmaein front
うしろushirobehind, back
なかnakainside
そとsotooutside
あいだaidabetween
ひだり / みぎhidari / migileft / right
ちかくchikakunear
となり / そば / よこtonari / soba / yokobeside
むこうmukouacross
きた / みなみ / にし / ひがしkita / minami / nishi / higashinorth / south / west / east

"Between" takes two things: honya to ginkou no aida (between the bookstore and the bank).

  • Kissaten wa honya to ginkou no aida ni arimasu. (The coffee shop is between the bookstore and the bank.)
  • Neko wa heya no soto ni imasu. (The cat is outside the room.)
  • Kuruma no kagi wa tsukue no ue ni arimasu ka. (Is the car key on top of the desk?)

Watch out

  • People and animals take imasu even when the sentence is about location: Ana san wa nihon ni imasu.
  • The place marker is ni. The wa in the first shape belongs to the thing you are talking about, not to the place.
  • Where and what use different words: Doko ni arimasu ka? (Where is it?) but Nani ga arimasu ka? (What is there?), as in Kaban no naka ni nani ga arimasu ka. (What is inside the bag?)
  • Keep the order inside position phrases: thing, no, position word. Never the other way round.
  • In ni (wa) ... ga arimasen, the wa only adds emphasis. The meaning stays the same.

Chapter 3: Counting, prices, phone numbers

Chapter 3 is mostly memory work: the numbers, a handful of sound changes, and a counter for each kind of thing.

Bigger numbers are stacked: 11 is juu ichi (ten and one), 20 is ni juu (two tens), 25 is ni juu go, 99 is kyuu juu kyuu.

The other hundreds and thousands follow the plain pattern: ni hyaku (200), yon hyaku (400), go hyaku (500), nana hyaku (700), kyuu hyaku (900), ni sen (2,000), yon sen, go sen, roku sen, nana sen, kyuu sen.

  • 11,500 is ichiman issen go hyaku.
  • 11,657 is ichiman issen roppyaku gojuu nana.
  • 1,500,000 is hyaku gojuu man, because 150 groups of ten thousand.

Prices

PatternMeaningExample
A wa ikura desu kaHow much is A?Kippu wa ikura desu ka. (How much is the ticket?)
A wa ikura gurai desu kaAround how much is A?Sono tokei wa ikura gurai desu ka. (Around how much is that watch?)
Amount + en / doru / pesoThe price, in yen, dollars or pesosKippu wa hyaku hachijuu en desu. (The ticket is 180 yen.)
Zenbu de ...In totalZenbu de sen doru desu. (Everything is 1,000 dollars.)

Checking a price works like any yes/no question: Sanbyaku gojuu en desu ka. Hai, sou desu. (Is it 350 yen? Yes, that's right.)

Phone numbers

Ask with Denwa bangou wa nan desu ka (or nanban desu ka). Say each digit on its own, say no for the hyphen, and say zero as zero, rei or maru.

  • 7326-5471 is nana san ni roku no go yon nana ichi.
  • For a cell phone, ask Keitai bangou wa nan desu ka.

Counters

In Japanese you count with a short ending that depends on what you are counting. You can put the counter after the noun or before it with no: ringo sanko and sanko no ringo both mean three apples.

Pages use pe-ji (nanpe-ji, what page). The sounds shift mostly on 1, 3, 6, 8 and 10 (ippon, sanbon, roppon, happon, juppon), so drill those. Age 20 is its own word, hatachi.

Counters work inside the sentence patterns you already know:

  • Otouto wa hatachi desu. (My younger brother is 20.)
  • Kyoushitsu ni gakusei ga juugonin imasu. (There are 15 students in the classroom.)
  • Kyoudai wa nannin desu ka. (How many siblings do you have?)
  • Anata wa nanbanme desu ka. (Which number child are you?)
  • Anata wa oikutsu desu ka. (How old are you? Nansai desu ka works too.)

Words worth locking in

nedan (price), yachin (rent), okane (money), en (yen), doru (dollar), zenbu (all, total), gurai (about), hatachi (20 years old), bangou (number), keitai bangou (cell phone number), denwa bangou (phone number), enpitsu (pencil), bo-rupen (ball pen), tegami (letter), kippu (ticket), kitte (postal stamp), kyoukasho (textbook), kasa (umbrella), bin (bottle), mikan (orange), ringo (apple), kyoudai (siblings).

Watch out

  • The numbers 4, 7 and 9 each have two readings. The book's phone numbers use yon, nana and kyuu, so treat those as the safe default.
  • Sen (1,000) turns into issen when a bigger number comes before it: ichiman issen go hyaku.
  • Big numbers group by four digits, so 100,000 is juu man (ten ten-thousands).
  • Sankai is three times, sangai is the third floor. Same ending, different sound.
  • In phone numbers, say each digit separately and say no for the hyphen.
  • Ask how many with nan plus the counter: nannin, nanbon, nansatsu, nanbiki, nandai.

Chapter 4: Time expressions

Chapter 4 is where hiragana takes over, and where you learn to say when something happens, from clock times to the day, month and year.

Sentence patterns

PatternMeaningExample
A は Time です (A wa Time desu)A is at, on or in that timeにほんごの クラスは すいようびです。 (Nihongo no kurasu wa suiyoubi desu.) The Japanese class is on Wednesday.
Time から (kara)fromくじ じゅうごふんから (kuji juugofun kara) from 9:15
Time まで (made)untilじゅうよっかまで (juuyokka made) until the 14th
ちょうど (choudo) Timeexactlyちょうど さんじ (choudo sanji) exactly 3 o'clock, or くじちょうど (kuji choudo) 9 o'clock exactly
Time ごろ (goro)aroundしちじごろ (shichiji goro) around 7 o'clock
Time + marker ですadds clarityじゅぎょうは さんがつから です。 (Jugyou wa sangatsu kara desu.) The class is from March.
A は いつ ですか (A wa itsu desu ka)When is A?かいしゃの やすみは いつ ですか。 (Kaisha no yasumi wa itsu desu ka.) When is the company holiday?

You can chain から and まで: ごご にじから ごじまで (gogo niji kara goji made) is from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.

11 and 12 o'clock are じゅういちじ (juuichiji) and じゅうにじ (juuniji). Fifteen minutes is じゅうごふん (juugofun) and thirty is さんじゅっぷん (sanjuppun). Ask with なんじ (nanji, what time) and なんぷん (nanpun, what minute).

Half past is はん (han): じゅうにじ はん (juuniji han) is 12:30. Say the bigger unit first, so 1:15 is いちじ じゅうごふん (ichiji juugofun). For a.m. and p.m., put ごぜん (gozen) or ごご (gogo) in front: ごぜん くじ (gozen kuji) is 9 a.m., ごご しちじ (gogo shichiji) is 7 p.m.

Months, dates and years

Months are the number plus がつ (gatsu): いちがつ (ichigatsu) through じゅうにがつ (juunigatsu). The three traps are April しがつ (shigatsu), July しちがつ (shichigatsu) and September くがつ (kugatsu). Ask with なんがつ (nangatsu).

Years are the number plus ねん (nen): 2018 is にせんじゅうはちねん (nisen juuhachinen) and 2024 is にせんにじゅうよねん (nisen nijuuyonen). Ask with なんねん (nannen). Dates run big to small: year, month, day. January 6 is いちがつ むいか (ichigatsu muika).

Everyまいにち (mainichi)まいしゅう (maishuu)まいつき (maitsuki)まいとし (maitoshi)

For mornings and nights: けさ (kesa) this morning, こんばん (konban) tonight, ゆうべ (yuube) last night, まいあさ (maiasa) every morning, まいばん (maiban) every night. For other days add の: きのうの あさ (kinou no asa) yesterday morning, あしたの よる (ashita no yoru) tomorrow night.

To attach one of these words to a day, connect them with の: らいしゅうの げつようび (raishuu no getsuyoubi) is next week Monday. Skip the の after まい (every): まいしゅう げつようび (maishuu getsuyoubi) is every Monday.

The four seasons: はる (haru) spring, March to May. なつ (natsu) summer, June to August. あき (aki) autumn, September to November. ふゆ (fuyu) winter, December to February.

Words worth locking in

Katakana shows up for borrowed words: クラス (kurasu), ミーティング (mi-tingu), パーティー (pa-ti-), プロジェクト (purojekuto), クリスマス (kurisumasu).

じゅぎょう / クラス (jugyou / kurasu) class, かいぎ / ミーティング (kaigi / mi-tingu) meeting, しごと (shigoto) work, しめきり (shimekiri) deadline, やすみ (yasumi) vacation, holiday, きゅうけい (kyuukei) break, たんじょうび (tanjoubi) birthday, よてい (yotei) schedule, しあい (shiai) game, match, しけん (shiken) examination, きせつ (kisetsu) season, なつやすみ (natsuyasumi) summer vacation, しゅうまつ (shuumatsu) weekend, へいじつ (heijitsu) weekday, じかん (jikan) time, いま (ima) now, まず / はじめに (mazu / hajime ni) first, つぎ (tsugi) next, あさ (asa) morning, ひる (hiru) noon, daytime, よる / ばん (yoru / ban) night.

Watch out

  • Goro goes with a point in time (しちじごろ, around 7 o'clock). Gurai, which you meet in Chapter 5, goes with a length of time.
  • Ji is o'clock and fun is minutes: さんじ (sanji) is 3 o'clock, さんぷん (sanpun) is 3 minutes.
  • Memorize the special readings: よじ, しちじ, くじ, and しがつ, しちがつ, くがつ.
  • Dates from the 11th on are number plus にち, except the 14th, 17th, 19th, 20th, 24th, 27th and 29th.
  • Go big to small: month then day, hour then minute. ごぜん and ごご come before the time.
  • Use の with non-specific times (らいしゅうの げつようび) but not with まい (まいしゅう げつようび).

Chapter 5: Span of time (how long)

Chapter 5 moves from a point on the clock (4 o'clock) to the length of something (4 hours), then covers travel time and cost.

The ending かん (kan) is optional after minutes, days, months and years. Hours and weeks always keep it: じかん, しゅうかん.

A few specials: 6 months is ろっかげつ (rokkagetsu) or はんとし (hantoshi, half a year). 8 months is はっかげつ (hakkagetsu) or はちかげつ (hachikagetsu). 10 months is じゅっかげつ (jukkagetsu). An hour and a half is いちじかんはん (ichijikan han). 15 days is じゅうごにち (juugonichi).

Vehicles

Add で after a vehicle to say "by": バスで (basu de). The exception is あるいて (aruite, on foot), which needs no で.

Words worth locking in

りゅうがくせい (ryuugakusei) student studying abroad, せいと (seito) student, クラスメイト (kurasumeito) classmate, メンバー (menba-) member, おうふく (oufuku) roundtrip, かたみち (katamichi) one way, ひとつき (hitotsuki) one month, グループ (guru-pu) group, しゅくだい (shukudai) homework, もんだい (mondai) problem, トレーニング (tore-ningu) training, ゼミ (zemi) seminar, アルバイト (arubaito) part-time job, ざんぎょう (zangyou) overtime, かいわ (kaiwa) conversation, ぶんぽう (bunpou) grammar.

Watch out

  • Point or length: よじ is 4 o'clock, よじかん is 4 hours. しがつ is April, よんかげつ is 4 months.
  • Gurai is for lengths (いちじかんぐらい). Goro, from Chapter 4, is for points in time (しちじごろ).
  • One verb, two kinds of question: かかります covers time and money. どのぐらい or なんじかん asks about time, いくら or いくらぐらい asks about money.
  • No で after あるいて.
  • Frequency uses に right after the span: いっしゅうかんに にかい.
  • Hours and weeks always keep かん (じかん, しゅうかん). With minutes, days, months and years it is optional.
  • まえ and すぎ follow the time: いちじ ごふんまえ is 5 minutes before 1.

Answer key

Most questions have more than one acceptable wording. These are the ones that match the patterns in the chapters.

#AnswerWhy
1waWa marks what you are talking about.
2Kim san wa kenshuusei dewa arimasen. / Kim san wa kenshuusei ja arimasen.Desu becomes dewa arimasen or ja arimasen.
3waMo turns into wa in a no answer.
4konoKono needs a noun after it (hon). Kore stands alone.
5Kono surippa wa dare no desu ka.Dare no means whose.
6imasuA cat is a living thing.
7Ginkou wa eki no mae ni arimasu.Thing, then no, then the position word.
8Anata no gakkou ni kafe ga arimasu ka.This asks whether something exists, so use the ga shape.
9The first tells you where the coffee shop is, and assumes you already know about it. The second tells you there is a coffee shop next to the bookstore.A wa Location ni arimasu answers "where?". Location ni A ga arimasu says what is there.
10Kaban no naka ni nani ga arimasu ka.Nan becomes nani before a marker.
11sanjuu roku30 plus 6.
12happyaku, sanzenBoth are special readings.
13ichiman issen go hyaku10,000 plus 1,000 plus 500. Sen becomes issen after a bigger number.
14nana san ni roku no go yon nana ichiOne digit at a time, and no for the hyphen.
15enpitsu sanbon, gakusei futariPencils are long and thin, so hon. Two people is futari.
16Kyoushitsu ni gakusei ga nannin imasu ka.Nannin counts people, and people take imasu.
17Kippu wa ikura desu ka. Hyaku hachijuu en desu.Ikura asks for a price.
18しがつ (shigatsu), よじ (yoji)Both are special readings.
19くじ じゅうごふんから じゅういちじはんまで (kuji juugofun kara juuichiji han made)Han means half past.
20らいしゅうの げつようび (raishuu no getsuyoubi), まいしゅう げつようび (maishuu getsuyoubi)の connects raishuu to the day, but not maishuu.
21ごろ (goro)Goro goes with a point in time. Gurai goes with a length.
22クラスは さんじから ろくじまでです。 (Kurasu wa sanji kara rokuji made desu.)Kara and made go right after the times.
23おかあさんの たんじょうびは いつですか。 (Okaasan no tanjoubi wa itsu desu ka.)Itsu means when.
24よじかん (yojikan), よじ (yoji)Kan turns a time on the clock into a length.
25さんかげつ (sankagetsu), さんがつ (sangatsu)Kagetsu counts months, gatsu names them.
26いっしゅうかんに にかい (isshuukan ni nikai)Span, then に, then how many times.
27ちかてつで さんじゅっぷん かかります。 (Chikatetsu de sanjuppun kakarimasu.)で marks the vehicle, かかります says it takes.
28しんかんせんで いくら かかりますか。 (Shinkansen de ikura kakarimasu ka.)Ikura asks about money.
29いちじ ごふんまえ (ichiji gofun mae)まえ comes after the time.
30いえから がっこうまで どのぐらい かかりますか。 (Ie kara gakkou made donogurai kakarimasu ka.)Donogurai asks about time.

Source: JLRC Intensive Japanese 1 workbook (Revised Edition, January 2022), Chapters 1 to 5.

docs.html:
How to use this reviewer

Every word from Chapters 1 to 5 is here, grouped the way each lesson teaches it, with the kana, the romaji and the meaning in English.

The best way to study it is to cover one column at a time:

  1. Cover the English column, read the Japanese, and say the meaning out loud.
  2. Cover the Japanese columns, read the English, and say the word.
  3. Note the ones you missed and go through only those again the next day.

When a list starts to feel easy, jump to the self-test near the end and write your answers in the table. Special readings and easy-to-mix-up pairs are noted under the tables.

Chapter 5: Span of time

Question 33

  • A: Uchi kara gakkou made nanpun kakarimasu ka.
  • B: ______ de 20-pun kakarimasu.

Choices: (a) Basu (b) Aruite (c) Oufuku (d) Katamichi

Question 34

  • A: Uchi kara kaisha made nanjikan kakarimasu ka.
  • B: ______ kakarimasu.
  • Note: It takes 2 hours.

Choices: (a) Niji (b) Nijikan (c) Nifun (d) Nijuppun

Question 35

  • A: Kaigi wa 3-ji desu.
  • B: Ima wa 2-ji 55-fun desu. Kaigi no 5-fun ______ desu.

Choices: (a) sugi (b) goro (c) mae (d) gurai

Question 36

  • A: Kaisha made jitensha de nanpun kakarimasu ka.
  • B: 15-fun ______ kakarimasu.

Choices: (a) goro (b) made (c) sugi (d) gurai

Question 37

  • A: Kippu wa ikura desu ka.
  • B: ______ wa 2,000-en desu. Katamichi wa 1,100-en desu.

Choices: (a) Oufuku (b) Katamichi (c) Norimono (d) Hitotsuki

Question 38

  • A: Nihon ni nannen imasu ka.
  • B: ______ imasu.
  • Note: Half a year.

Choices: (a) Hitotsuki (b) Hantoshi (c) Ichinen (d) Ichijikan

Question 39

  • A: Kaisha wa 5-ji made desu ne.
  • B: Hai. Demo kyou wa 8-ji made shigoto desu. ______ desu.

Choices: (a) Shukudai (b) Arubaito (c) Zangyou (d) Kaiwa

Question 40

  • A: Manira kara Toukyou made ______ de 4-jikan gurai kakarimasu.

Choices: (a) fune (b) jitensha (c) chikatetsu (d) hikouki

Answer key for Exam 1

#AnswerWhy
1(a) DouzoAfter hajimemashite, the set phrase is douzo yoroshiku onegaishimasu. It is what you say when you meet someone for the first time.
2(b) noNo links two nouns and shows who or what something belongs to. Sakura-kaisha no shachou means the president of Sakura company.
3(c) dokoDoko asks where. Dare is who, dore is which one and itsu is when. Otearai (washroom) is a place, so you ask doko.
4(d) chuugokugoAdd go to the country name to get the language: chuugoku becomes chuugokugo. English is the odd one out (eigo).
5(a) aniFor your own family use the plain words: ani, ane, chichi, haha. Oniisan is for someone else's older brother, ane is your own older sister and otouto is your own younger brother.
6(b) KoreKore is for things near the speaker, and B is the one holding it. Sore would be the thing near A, are is far from both, and dore is the question word.
7(c) kataKata is the polite word for person, and donata is the polite word for who, so they go together. Kore, koko and dochira mean this, here and which way.
8(d) Mou ichidoMou ichido onegaishimasu means again, please. It is what you say in class when you did not catch something.
9(a) migiMigi (right) is the opposite of hidari (left).
10(b) nishiOsaka is to the west of Tokyo, so the word is nishi. Higashi is east, kita is north and minami is south.
11(c) imasuTanaka-san and Maria-san are people, and people take imasu. Arimasu is for things. Imasen would say that nobody is there, which does not fit since two names were given.
12(d) arimasuA key and eyeglasses are things, so the verb is arimasu. People and animals use imasu.
13(a) kafeKissaten and kafe mean the same thing: coffee shop. Depa-to is a department store, honya is a bookstore and resutoran is a restaurant.
14(b) ryouRyou is a dormitory, a place where someone can be. Do not mix it up with ryoushin, which means parents.
15(c) tonariYoko, tonari and soba all mean beside in the book, so B is agreeing with tonari. Mukou is across, ushiro is behind and shita is under.
16(d) aidaAida means between, and it is used with two things: ginkou to kafe no aida.
17(a) Happyaku-en800 is happyaku. The hundreds 300, 600 and 800 change their sound: sanbyaku, roppyaku and happyaku.
18(b) YonsatsuSatsu is the counter for books and notebooks. Mai is for flat, thin things like paper, hon is for long things like pencils and ko is for small objects.
19(c) FutariAni and watashi make two people, and two people is futari. It is one of the special readings, so learn it as its own word, like hitori for one person.
20(d) HassaiEight years old is hassai. The sound changes, so it is not hachisai.
21(a) nedanNedan means price. Yachin is rent for a room or house, kippu is a ticket and okane is money in general.
22(b) Sanzen-en3,000 is sanzen. The special thousands are 1,000 (sen or issen), 3,000 (sanzen) and 8,000 (hassen).
23(c) Juuniman-enJapanese counts in groups of four digits. 120,000 is 12 ten-thousands: juu ni man.
24(d) zenbuZenbu means all or total. The apple and the orange together come to 300 yen in all.
25(a) mokuyoubiIf today is Wednesday (suiyoubi), tomorrow is Thursday, mokuyoubi.
26(b) KugatsuSeptember is kugatsu. Nine is ku in the month names, not kyuu. Kugetsu would mean nine months.
27(c) hatsukaThe 20th has its own reading, hatsuka. It does not follow the usual nichi pattern.
28(d) yoji4 o'clock is yoji. The hour four becomes yo, so it is not yonji or shiji.
29(a) goroGoro goes with a point in time and means around. Gurai is for amounts, like about 20 minutes. Han would make it 10:30.
30(b) madeKara means from and made means until. Gozen 9-ji kara gogo 6-ji made is from 9 a.m. until 6 p.m.
31(c) raigetsuIf this month is October, the next month is raigetsu. Sengetsu is last month, kongetsu is this month and maitsuki is every month.
32(d) kinouToday is the 10th (tooka), so the 9th (kokonoka) was yesterday, kinou. Ototoi is the day before yesterday.
33(a) BasuDe goes after a vehicle: basu de means by bus. Aruite already means on foot, so it never takes de. Oufuku and katamichi are about tickets.
34(b) NijikanKan marks how long something lasts. Nijikan is two hours. Niji would be 2 o'clock, nifun is two minutes and nijuppun is twenty minutes.
35(c) maeMae means before. 2:55 is five minutes before the 3:00 meeting, so 5-fun mae. Sugi means after.
36(d) guraiGurai means about and goes with an amount of time, here about 15 minutes. Goro goes with a point in time instead.
37(a) OufukuKatamichi (one way) is already named in the next sentence, so the first word is oufuku, round trip. It costs more because you travel both ways.
38(b) HantoshiHantoshi is half a year. Hitotsuki is one month, ichinen is one year and ichijikan is one hour.
39(c) ZangyouZangyou is overtime. The company closes at 5 but the work goes on until 8. Shukudai is homework, arubaito is a part-time job and kaiwa is conversation.
40(d) hikoukiHikouki is an airplane. Manila to Tokyo takes about four hours by plane. A ship would take days, and a bicycle or subway cannot cross the sea.

Exam 2: Reading, Chapters 1 to 5

II. Read each passage, then choose the best answer to each question. Each question is worth 1 point.

Three short passages in simple Japanese: a self-introduction, a shop sign and a work week. A few words carry the reading in parentheses, the way your book shows furigana. The choices are in kana.

Passage 1

わたしの名前(なまえ)は マリアです。フィリピンじんです。いま、日本(にほん)の だいがくの りゅうがくせいです。

ともだちの ジョンさんは アメリカじんです。エンジニアです。

わたしの へやは だいがくの りょうに あります。へやの なかに つくえと いすが あります。つくえの うえに パソコンが あります。つくえの したに かばんが あります。

Question 1. マリアさんは なにじんですか。

Choices: (a) フィリピンじん (b) にほんじん (c) アメリカじん (d) ドイツじん

Question 2. ジョンさんの しごとは なんですか。

Choices: (a) せんせい (b) エンジニア (c) がくせい (d) しゃちょう

Question 3. マリアさんの へやは どこに ありますか。

Choices: (a) かいしゃ (b) えき (c) だいがくの りょう (d) としょかん

Question 4. かばんは どこに ありますか。

Choices: (a) つくえの うえ (b) いすの うえ (c) へやの そと (d) つくえの した

Question 5. つくえの うえに なにが ありますか。

Choices: (a) パソコン (b) かばん (c) いす (d) テレビ

Passage 2

ほんや ミナミ

ノートは 1さつ 120えんです。

ボールペンは 1ぽん 100えんです。

えんぴつは 5ほんで 250えんです。

ごぜん 9じから ごご 7じまで。

やすみは 日曜日(にちようび)です。

Question 6. ノートは 1さつ いくらですか。

Choices: (a) 100えん (b) 120えん (c) 150えん (d) 250えん

Question 7. えんぴつは 1ぽん いくらですか。

Choices: (a) 25えん (b) 100えん (c) 50えん (d) 250えん

Question 8. ノート 1さつと ボールペン 1ぽんは ぜんぶで いくらですか。

Choices: (a) 120えん (b) 170えん (c) 370えん (d) 220えん

Question 9. ほんやは なんじまでですか。

Choices: (a) ごご 7じ (b) ごぜん 9じ (c) ごご 9じ (d) ごぜん 7じ

Question 10. ほんやの やすみは なんようびですか。

Choices: (a) げつようび (b) にちようび (c) どようび (d) きんようび

Passage 3

わたしは マニラの かいしゃの かいしゃいんです。うちから かいしゃまで ちかてつで 40ぷんぐらい かかります。

かいしゃは ごぜん 8じはんから ごご 5じまでです。まいしゅう 月曜日(げつようび)の ごご 2じに かいぎが あります。

らいしゅうの 金曜日(きんようび)は やすみです。

Question 11. うちから かいしゃまで なんぷんぐらい かかりますか。

Choices: (a) 14ぷん (b) 4じかん (c) 40ぷん (d) 50ぷん

Question 12. かいしゃは なんじからですか。

Choices: (a) ごぜん 8じ (b) ごご 8じはん (c) ごぜん 9じ (d) ごぜん 8じはん

Question 13. かいぎは いつですか。

Choices: (a) まいしゅう げつようびの ごご 2じ (b) まいしゅう かようびの ごご 2じ (c) まいしゅう げつようびの ごぜん 2じ (d) らいしゅう げつようびの ごご 2じ

Question 14. らいしゅうの やすみは なんようびですか。

Choices: (a) げつようび (b) きんようび (c) かようび (d) どようび

Answer key for Exam 2

#AnswerWhy
1(a) フィリピンじんThe passage says フィリピンじんです, so Maria is Filipino. アメリカじん is John.
2(b) エンジニアJohn is described with エンジニアです, so he is an engineer.
3(c) だいがくの りょうへやは だいがくの りょうに あります. Ryou means dormitory, and the room is in the university dormitory.
4(d) つくえの したつくえの したに かばんが あります. Shita means under, so the bag is under the desk.
5(a) パソコンつくえの うえに パソコンが あります. Ue means on top, so the computer is on the desk.
6(b) 120えんノートは 1さつ 120えんです. The 100 yen is for the ballpen and 250 yen is for five pencils.
7(c) 50えん250 yen buys 5 pencils (5ほん). 250 divided by 5 is 50 yen each.
8(d) 220えんThe notebook is 120 yen and the ballpen is 100 yen. Together that is 220 yen. ぜんぶで means in total.
9(a) ごご 7じごご 7じまで means until 7 p.m. Gogo is p.m. and made means until. The 9 is the opening hour.
10(b) にちようびやすみは にちようびです. The kanji in the sign, 日曜日, is read にちようび, which is Sunday.
11(c) 40ぷん40ぷんぐらい かかります means it takes about 40 minutes. ぐらい means about, and かかります means it takes.
12(d) ごぜん 8じはんごぜん 8じはんから means from 8:30 a.m. Han means half past, so 8じはん is 8:30.
13(a) まいしゅう げつようびの ごご 2じまいしゅう げつようびの ごご 2じ means every Monday at 2 p.m. Maishuu is every week, not next week (らいしゅう).
14(b) きんようびらいしゅうの きんようびは やすみです. Next week's Friday is a day off. Monday is the meeting day, not the day off.

English translations of the passages

Passage 1. My name is Maria. I am Filipino. Right now I am an international student at a university in Japan. My friend John is American. He is an engineer. My room is in the university dormitory. In the room there is a desk and a chair. On top of the desk there is a computer. Under the desk there is a bag.

Passage 2. Minami Bookstore. Notebooks are 120 yen each. Ballpens are 100 yen each. Pencils are 250 yen for five. Open from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. Closed on Sundays.

Passage 3. I am an employee of a company in Manila. It takes about 40 minutes from my house to the company by subway. The company runs from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Every week there is a meeting on Monday at 2 p.m. Next week's Friday is a day off.

docs.title: Hiragana and Katakana Reviewer
docs.intro: Hiragana and katakana are the same 46 sounds written two ways, so once the first set clicks, the second goes much faster.
docs.html:
Hiragana and katakana are the same 46 sounds written two ways, so once the first set clicks, the second goes much faster.

How to use this reviewer

Your book uses romaji for the first three chapters, so kana is the skill that unlocks everything after it. Work through this doc in order:

  1. Learn one row of pairs at a time, about 4 to 6 sounds a day. Each row shows the hiragana and katakana together.
  2. Say the sound out loud while you write both characters by hand, three times each.
  3. Cover the romaji in the side-by-side chart, read both characters, then check yourself.
  4. Read the memory hook for each pair once, then try to recall it the next day without looking.
  5. Add the marks and blended sounds once the basic 46 pairs feel easy.
  6. Finish with the look-alike pairs, the words from your chapters and the self-test.

Which script is used for what. Hiragana is for Japanese words and grammar bits like wa, no and desu. Katakana is for foreign words, foreign names and emphasis, like パソコン (personal computer) and マニラ (Manila).

The five vowels never change. Every kana is a vowel on its own or a consonant plus one of these, so learn them first.

VowelSounds likeExample from your book
aah, as in fatherashita (tomorrow)
iee, as in seeinu (dog)
uoo, as in food, with relaxed lipsuchi (house)
eeh, as in peteki (train station)
ooh, as in more, but shorterokane (money)

Habits that help. Write by hand, because your fingers remember shapes your eyes forget. Study in two short sessions a day instead of one long one. Use the memory hooks below, then drop each hook as soon as you can read that character without it.

Hiragana and katakana side by side

Every cell shows the hiragana first, then the katakana, then the sound, so you learn each pair as one unit. Hiragana is round and flowing. Katakana is the same sound drawn with sharper, straighter strokes.

Rowaiueo
vowelsあ ア · aい イ · iう ウ · uえ エ · eお オ · o
kか カ · kaき キ · kiく ク · kuけ ケ · keこ コ · ko
sさ サ · saし シ · shiす ス · suせ セ · seそ ソ · so
tた タ · taち チ · chiつ ツ · tsuて テ · teと ト · to
nな ナ · naに ニ · niぬ ヌ · nuね ネ · neの ノ · no
hは ハ · haひ ヒ · hiふ フ · fuへ ヘ · heほ ホ · ho
mま マ · maみ ミ · miむ ム · muめ メ · meも モ · mo
yや ヤ · yaゆ ユ · yuよ ヨ · yo
rら ラ · raり リ · riる ル · ruれ レ · reろ ロ · ro
wわ ワ · waを ヲ · o

One more pair stands alone: ん ン · n. It is the only kana that is a consonant with no vowel.

Four sounds break the pattern in both scripts: shi (し シ), chi (ち チ), tsu (つ ツ) and fu (ふ フ). The r row sits between an English r, l and d, so tap your tongue once on the roof of your mouth. を ヲ is pronounced o, and を is only a grammar particle. ヲ is very rare, so do not spend time on it.

Memory hooks for each pair

Each hook ties the hiragana and the katakana to one picture, so the second character comes almost free once you know the first. Pairs marked Twin look nearly the same in both scripts. If a hook does not stick, make up your own: a silly image you invented beats a good one you borrowed.

Vowels, k row and s row

SoundHiraganaKatakanaMemory hook
aあアあ is an apple with a stem. ア is the axe that splits it.
iいイい is two eels side by side. イ is a tall eel leaning on a pole.
uうウBoth wear a hat. う has a small hat on a tilted U. ウ has a bigger hat on straight sides.
eえエえ is an exotic bird with a long tail. エ is an I-beam, like the shaft of an elevator (エレベーター).
oおオお is a person with a round belly saying "oh!" オ is the same person with the belly cut off.
kaかカTwin. か is a karate chop with a small flick. カ is the same chop, straightened.
kiきキTwin. A key with teeth. キ is the same key drawn with straight lines. Ki sounds like key.
kuくクく is a cuckoo's open beak. ク is the beak with a short roof stroke on top.
keけケけ is a keg of beer with a tap on its side. ケ is the keg tipped over, with the left stroke leaning.
koこコこ is two koi fish, one above the other. コ is a corner, squeezing the fish into a box.
saさサTwin. さ is a samurai holding a sword. サ is the same samurai with a straight sword.
shiしシし is a fishing hook. シ is two dots lying down like eyes and a smile swooping up. She smiles.
suすスす is a piece of sushi with a curl of rice. ス is a super hero's cape blowing in the wind.
seせセTwin. せ is a seesaw with a long plank. セ is the same plank with straight edges, like a chair seat.
soそソそ is a zigzag of sewing thread. ソ is the needle with a dot above and a long slanted stroke.

T row, n row and h row

SoundHiraganaKatakanaMemory hook
taたタた is the letters t and a squeezed together. タ is a table (ta-ble) with a slanted leg.
chiちチち looks like a 5, so picture five slices of cheese. チ looks like the kanji 千, the number thousand.
tsuつツつ is a tsunami wave curling over. ツ is three splashes of spray flying up from it.
teてテて is an open hand. The kanji for hand, 手, is read te. テ is a TV antenna, and it starts テレビ.
toとトと is a toe with a thorn stuck in it. ト is a totem pole with one arm out.
naなナな is a nun kneeling in prayer. ナ is just her cross.
niにニBoth look like 二, the number two, which is read ni. に has two lines on the right and ニ is two lines.
nuぬヌぬ is a noodle wound around a chopstick. ヌ is the same noodle, pinched into a sharp bend.
neねネね is a cat (neko) with a curled tail. ネ is the knot of a necktie, and it starts ネクタイ.
noのノの is a circle with a swish, like a sign saying no. ノ is just the slash across it.
haはハは is a person laughing out loud, ha ha. ハ is a hat (ha-t) with two sloping sides.
hiひヒひ is a wide grin, hee hee. ヒ is a heel, the side view of a bent foot.
fuふフふ is Mount Fuji with a patch of cloud. フ is a flag hanging from a pole.
heへヘTwin, and almost identical. Both are a hill. "Hey, a hill!"
hoほホほ is は with an extra bar, like Santa laughing ho ho ho. ホ is a Christmas tree.

M row, y row, r row, w row and n

SoundHiraganaKatakanaMemory hook
maまマま is a mama with her arms out and a bundle at her feet. マ is a mallet, with a flat head and a slanted handle.
miみミみ is a number 3 with a tail. ミ is three slanted lines. Mittsu means three, so both are 3.
muむムむ is a cow saying moo, with a small horn on the right. ム is the cow's pointed snout and horn.
meめメめ is an eye. The kanji for eye, 目, is read me. メ is an X over the eye, like X marks me.
moもモも is a fish hook with two worms. モ is the same hook, straightened. You want mo(re) worms.
yaやヤや is a yak with a long horn on top. ヤ is a yacht with a tall mast and a slanted sail.
yuゆユゆ is a fish swimming in a hot spring. Yu means hot water. ユ is a U-shaped pool with a floor line.
yoよヨよ is a yo-yo on its string. ヨ is a backwards E with three bars.
raらラら is a rabbit sitting with one ear up. ラ is the rabbit from behind, with two bars for ears and a curved back.
riりリTwin. り is two reeds by a river bank. リ is the same two reeds, shorter and straighter.
ruるルる is a road that ends in a small loop. ル is two legs running. Ru-n.
reれレれ is ね with the loop taken out, so it has been re-moved. レ is a check mark, as in re-ceived.
roろロろ is a plain road (ro-ad) with no loop. ロ is a box, a room (ro-om) with four walls.
waわワわ is someone shouting "wa!" in surprise. ワ is ウ without its hat, a water (wa-ter) glass with no lid.
oをヲを is an acrobat in mid-air, "woah!" ヲ is the same acrobat drawn with straight lines, and very rare.
nんンん is a cursive lowercase n. ン starts low on the left and sweeps upward, like an n heading uphill.

Marks and blended sounds, side by side

Two dots make a sound voiced, a small circle turns h into p, and a small ya, yu or yo blends two kana into one sound. The marks work the same way in both scripts, so you learn them once.

Two dots and the small circle

The two dots (dakuten) go on the k, s, t and h rows. The small circle (handakuten) goes only on the h row.

Rowaiueo
gが ガ · gaぎ ギ · giぐ グ · guげ ゲ · geご ゴ · go
zざ ザ · zaじ ジ · jiず ズ · zuぜ ゼ · zeぞ ゾ · zo
dだ ダ · daぢ ヂ · jiづ ヅ · zuで デ · deど ド · do
bば バ · baび ビ · biぶ ブ · buべ ベ · beぼ ボ · bo
pぱ パ · paぴ ピ · piぷ プ · puぺ ペ · peぽ ポ · po

The d row has two odd ones. ぢ ヂ sounds exactly like じ ジ, and づ ヅ sounds exactly like ず ズ. They are rare, so when you write ji or zu yourself, use じ and ず.

Blended sounds with a small ya, yu or yo

Write the second kana smaller and a little lower right. The pair is one beat, not two.

Startyayuyo
kiきゃ キャ · kyaきゅ キュ · kyuきょ キョ · kyo
shiしゃ シャ · shaしゅ シュ · shuしょ ショ · sho
chiちゃ チャ · chaちゅ チュ · chuちょ チョ · cho
niにゃ ニャ · nyaにゅ ニュ · nyuにょ ニョ · nyo
hiひゃ ヒャ · hyaひゅ ヒュ · hyuひょ ヒョ · hyo
miみゃ ミャ · myaみゅ ミュ · myuみょ ミョ · myo
riりゃ リャ · ryaりゅ リュ · ryuりょ リョ · ryo
giぎゃ ギャ · gyaぎゅ ギュ · gyuぎょ ギョ · gyo
jiじゃ ジャ · jaじゅ ジュ · juじょ ジョ · jo
biびゃ ビャ · byaびゅ ビュ · byuびょ ビョ · byo
piぴゃ ピャ · pyaぴゅ ピュ · pyuぴょ ピョ · pyo

Size matters: きゃ is one beat (kya), but きや with a full-size や is two beats (ki-ya). You will see blended sounds in your book in しゅくだい (shukudai, homework), りょうしん (ryoushin, parents), じゅぎょう (jugyou, class) and びょういん (byouin, hospital).

Sound rules that trip people up

Five rules cover almost every reading mistake beginners make, and each one applies to both scripts.

1. Small tsu (っ ッ) doubles the next consonant. You hold a tiny pause before it. がっこう is gak-kou (school), きっぷ is kip-pu (ticket) and きって is kit-te (postal stamp). In katakana, ベッド is bed-do (bed) and カップ is kap-pu (cup).

2. Long vowels last twice as long. Hiragana adds a vowel kana. Katakana uses a dash called ー.

Long soundHow to write itExample from your book
aaadd あおかあさん (okaasan, mother)
iiadd いおにいさん (oniisan, older brother)
uuadd うしゅうまつ (shuumatsu, weekend)
eeadd え, or い after eおねえさん (oneesan, older sister) and せんせい (sensei, teacher)
ooadd お or うおおさか (oosaka, Osaka) and こうじょう (koujou, factory)
any, in katakanaadd ーコンピューター (kompyu-ta-, computer) and ノート (no-to, notebook)

Length changes the word. おばさん (obasan) is an aunt and おばあさん (obaasan) is a grandmother.

3. ん ン is a full beat of its own. こんにちは is ko-n-ni-chi-wa, five beats. Do not rush it.

4. Three hiragana change sound as grammar words. は is read wa, へ is read e and を is read o, but only when they act as particles. わたしはマリアです is watashi wa Maria desu. Katakana has no such cases.

5. The u in です and ます is nearly silent. です sounds like "dess" and あります sounds like "arimass." You still write the す.

Katakana-only sounds for foreign words

Katakana has extra combinations so Japanese can write sounds that do not exist in native words. Hiragana does not need these. A small vowel (ァ ィ ェ ォ) after a full-size kana blends with it into one beat.

KatakanaSoundExample
ファ フィ フェ フォfa, fi, fe, foフィリピン (firipin, Philippines), カフェ (kafe, café), フォーク (fo-ku, fork)
ティ ディti, diパーティー (pa-ti-, party), ディナー (dina-, dinner)
ウィ ウェ ウォwi, we, woウェブ (webu, web), ウォーター (uo-ta-, water)
シェ ジェ チェshe, je, cheシェア (shea, share), ジェット (jetto, jet), チェック (chekku, check)
ヴァ ヴィ ヴ ヴェ ヴォva, vi, vu, ve, voヴァイオリン (vaiorin, violin). Many words use バ ビ ブ ベ ボ instead.

You can read most of these by sounding them out: the big kana gives the consonant and the small vowel gives the vowel. ティ is te plus a small i, so it says ti.

Look-alikes and how to tell them apart

A small set of pairs causes most reading mistakes. Look for the one detail that separates each pair, and quiz yourself on these first.

Hiragana pairs

PairThe difference
し / つし is tall and hooks upward at the bottom, like a fishing hook. つ is wide and flat on top, curving over and down on the right, like a wave.
ぬ / めぬ ends in a loop at the bottom right, like the end of a noodle. め ends in a point.
ね / れ / わね ends in a loop, the cat's tail. れ ends in an open kick with no loop. わ ends in a round curl that turns back in.
は / ほほ has one extra bar across the top of the right side.
る / ろる ends in a loop and ろ does not.
あ / おお has a small dot at the top right and あ does not.
い / りIn い the left stroke is the longer one. In り the right stroke is the longer one.
こ / にに has a tall stroke on the left. こ is just two bars.

Katakana pairs

PairThe difference
シ / ツシ has dots that lie sideways and a swoosh that sweeps up like a smile. ツ has dots that stand upright and a long stroke that falls down to the left.
ソ / ンソ has a long stroke that falls down to the left. ン has a long stroke that starts low and rises to the right.
ク / タタ is ク with one extra slash inside it.
ウ / ワウ has a small hat on top. ワ has no hat.
コ / ユコ is open on the left like a corner. ユ has a bottom line that sticks out past the box.

Katakana that look like kanji

Real Japanese text mixes kanji in, so these will show up. If the character sits inside a word made of katakana, it is katakana.

KatakanaLooks likeKanji meaning
カ ka力power (chikara)
ロ ro口mouth (kuchi)
エ e工craft or work (kou)
ニ ni二two (ni)
ハ ha八eight (hachi)
タ ta夕evening (yuu)
ミ mi三three (san)

These are the answers to all 89 exercise items in the Chapter 6 workbook, in page order. Part V asks about you, so it gives sample answers you can swap for your own.

Noun past tense (page 88)

Change です to でした, and じゃありません to じゃありませんでした.

#AnswerMeaning
1でんわばんごうは 8812-3565 でした。The phone number was 8812-3565.
2がっこうのやすみは とおかかんでした。The school break was ten days.
3かようびは しけんでした。Tuesday was the exam.
4げつようびは やすみじゃありませんでした。Monday was not a day off.
5キムさんは エンジニアじゃありませんでした。Kim was not an engineer.

Adjective conjugation tables (page 92)

For い-adjectives, drop the final い and add くない, かった or くなかった. For な-adjectives, treat them like nouns: です, じゃありません, でした, じゃありませんでした. The first row of each table was already done in the book.

い-adjectives

Present positivePresent negativePast positivePast negative
あかるい(です)あかるくない(です)あかるかった(です)あかるくなかった(です)
ちかい(です)ちかくない(です)ちかかった(です)ちかくなかった(です)
ながい(です)ながくない(です)ながかった(です)ながくなかった(です)
あつい(です)あつくない(です)あつかった(です)あつくなかった(です)
みじかい(です)みじかくない(です)みじかかった(です)みじかくなかった(です)
やすい(です)やすくない(です)やすかった(です)やすくなかった(です)

な-adjectives

Present positivePresent negativePast positivePast negative

にぎやかですにぎやかじゃありませんにぎやかでしたにぎやかじゃありませんでした

じゃありません can also be written ではありません in every な-adjective row.

Change to negative (page 93)

Keep the tense of the sentence. Items 5 and 7 are already past, so their negatives stay past.

#AnswerMeaning
1クリスマスパーティーは にぎやかじゃありません。The Christmas party is not lively.
2そのみちは ひろくないです。That road is not wide.
3けいたいは かるくないです。The cell phone is not light.
4そのコーヒーは あつくないです。That coffee is not hot.
5どようびは ひまじゃありませんでした。I was not free on Saturday.
6そのりょうりは ゆうめいじゃありません。That dish is not famous.
7コンピュータは たかくなかったです。The computer was not expensive.
8げつようびは いそがしくないです。I am not busy on Monday.
9そのみせは べんりじゃありません。That shop is not convenient.
10かんじは むずかしくないです。Kanji is not difficult.
11しけんは かんたんじゃありません。The exam is not easy.

Change to past tense (page 93)

For い-adjectives use かったです, or くなかったです for the negative. For な-adjectives use でした.

#AnswerMeaning
1いえは ちかくなかったです。The house was not near.
2しけんは むずかしかったです。The exam was difficult.
3しゅくだいは かんたんでした。The homework was easy.
4そのほんは おもしろかったです。That book was interesting.
5かようびは いそがしかったです。Tuesday was busy.
6にほんごの ほんは うすくなかったです。The Japanese book was not thin.
7けいたいは たかくなかったです。The cell phone was not expensive.
8かいぎしつは しずかでした。The conference room was quiet.
9あのところは にぎやかでした。That place was lively.
10きゅうけいは ながくなかったです。The break was not long.
11パーティーは たのしかったです。The party was fun.

Choose the adjective (page 94)

Each word in the box is used exactly once. The adjective before the blank (むずかしくて, かるくて, きれいで) sets the mood, so the word you pick has to pair naturally with it.

#AnswerFull sentence
1つまらないえいごの クラスは むずかしくて つまらないです。 (The English class is difficult and boring.)
2ひろいこのへやは あかるくて ひろいです。 (This room is bright and wide.)
3ちいさいわたしのけいたいは かるくて ちいさいです。 (My cell phone is light and small.)
4あぶないこのみちは くらくて あぶないです。 (This road is dark and dangerous.)
5しずかこのアパートは きれいで しずかな ところに あります。 (This apartment is in a clean and quiet place.)
6やさしいすずきせんせいは あかるくて やさしい ひとです。 (Mr. Suzuki is a bright and kind person.)
7おもいこのほんは おおきくて おもいです。 (This book is big and heavy.)
8さむいにほんのふゆは さむいです。 (Winter in Japan is cold.)
9かんたんこのもんだいのこたえは かんたんです。 (The answer to this problem is easy.)
10まずいあのレストランは たかくて まずいです。 (That restaurant is expensive and tastes bad.)

The box has さむい, おもい, やさしい, つまらない, あぶない, かんたん, ひろい, まずい, しずか, ちいさい. All ten are placed above.

Review I, choose the grammar pattern (page 96)

#AnswerWhy
14 おいしくなかったThe question is about yesterday, so past tense, and あまり needs a negative ending.
24 どんなどんな plus a noun asks "what kind of", and the reply describes the person.
31 きれいなA な-adjective keeps な before a noun.
43 おもしろくてTo connect い-adjectives, drop い and add くて.
52 いそがしくないあまり needs a negative, and the question is present tense.
63 とてもあまり needs a negative ending, but べんりです is positive, so use とても.
74 きれいでTo connect な-adjectives, add で.
81 むずかしいAn い-adjective goes straight before a noun with no extra ending.

Review II, rearrange the words (page 97)

The order column lists which word number goes in blanks 1 to 4. The book prints no star box, so the full sentence is shown too.

#OrderFull sentenceMeaning
14 1 3 2この へやは せまくて ふるいです。This room is small and old.
21 4 2 3あたらしい ぶちょうは どんな ひとですか。What kind of person is the new department head?
34 2 1 3あれは おおきくて おもい テレビです。That is a big, heavy TV.
43 2 4 1この りょうりは あまり おいしくないです。This dish is not very tasty.
52 4 3 1きょうしつの なかに ながい テーブルが あります。There is a long table in the classroom.
63 1 4 2いえの ちかくに ひろくて しずかな こうえんが あります。There is a wide, quiet park near my house.
72 4 1 3せんせいは きれいで やさしい ひとです。The teacher is a pretty, kind person.
83 1 2 4きょうの テストは たいへん むずかしかったです。Today's test was very difficult.

Review III and IV, fill in and reading (pages 98 and 99)

ItemAnswerWhy
III (1)3 ちかいThe office is a five minute walk away, so the apartment is very near.
III (2)2 せまいThe room is a little small, and the toilet and kitchen are small too.
III (3)1 ゆうめいなA famous park next to the apartment is the only choice that fits before こうえん.
IV 13 にほんのきせつは よっつですThe text lists four seasons: はる, なつ, あき, ふゆ.
IV 22 まいにち あついですThe text says なつは まいにち たいへん あついです.

Review V, answer in sentences (page 100)

These questions are about you, so there is no single right answer. Any reply works if the adjective ending is correct and it answers what was asked. Use くない or じゃありません for "no".

#Sample answerAnother way to answer
1きょうのてんきは いいです。きょうのてんきは わるいです。
2はい、ひまです。いいえ、ひまじゃありません。
3はい、とおいです。いいえ、とおくないです。
4しずかです。にぎやかです。
5ちょっと むずかしいです。とても たのしいです。
6やさしい ひとです。きれいな ひとです。
7むずかしいです。あまり むずかしくないです。
8はい、むずかしいです。いいえ、あまり むずかしくないです。
9はい、とても おいしいです。いいえ、あまり おいしくないです。
10いいえ、ひろくないです。ちょっと せまいです。はい、ひろいです。

Review VI, translate to Japanese (page 100)

#JapaneseNote
1あの たてものは とても たかいです。あの is "that one over there". たいへん also works for "very".
2こうえんは わたしのいえから とおいです。から means "from".
3これは おおきくて おもい ほんです。おおきい becomes おおきくて to connect to おもい.
4かんじのしけんは あまり むずかしくなかったです。あまり plus a past negative.
5わたしのアルバイトは おもしろくないです。つまらないです also works.
6しけんは むずかしかったです。Past tense of むずかしい.
7わたしは こんしゅう いそがしいです。こんしゅう means "this week".
8かいぎは ながいですか。Add か to make it a question.
9きのうは あつかったですか。いいえ、さむかったです。These are the weather words for hot and cold. いいえ、あつくなかったです。さむかったです。 is also fine.

docs.intro: Every Chapter 6 word is here: the 24 from the vocabulary list, the adjectives taught in the grammar pages, and the few extra words that show up in the exercises. Adjectives get the most room because they are what this whole chapter is about.
docs.html:
Every Chapter 6 word is here: the 24 from the vocabulary list, the adjectives taught in the grammar pages, and the few extra words that show up in the exercises. Adjectives get the most room because they are what this whole chapter is about.

How to use this reviewer

  • Cover the English column, read the Japanese, and say the meaning out loud.
  • Cover the Japanese columns, read the English, and say the word.
  • Mark the ones you missed and go through only those again the next day.
  • When the lists start to feel easy, jump to the self-test at the end.

Chapter 6: Adjectives

The book's vocabulary list for this chapter has 24 words. It groups them as places, home words, study words, a few adverbs and one food word.

Places

KanaRomajiEnglish
ところ・ばしょtokoro / bashoplace
たてもの・ビルtatemono / birubuilding
こうえんkouenpark
みちmichiroad
くうこうkuukouairport
みなとminatoharbor, seaport
(お)みせ(o)misestore, shop
くすりやkusuriyadrugstore, pharmacy

Tokoro and basho both mean place. Tatemono is the Japanese word for building, and biru is the short form of the English word. Kuukou is literally an air harbor: kuu is air and kou is harbor, the same harbor as minato. Kusuriya is kusuri (medicine) plus ya (shop), the same ya as honya (bookstore) from Chapter 2.

Home and food

KanaRomajiEnglish
トイレtoiretoilet
だいどころdaidokorokitchen
ベッドbeddobed
りょうりryouridish, cooking

Toire and beddo come from English, so they are written in katakana. Ryouri means both the dish itself and the act of cooking.

Study and writing

KanaRomajiEnglish
べんきょうbenkyoustudy
れんしゅうrenshuupractice
テスト・しけんtesuto / shikentest, examination
こたえkotaeanswer
かんじkanjiChinese character
じjicharacter, letter
メモmemomemo
しゃしんshashinpicture

Tesuto and shiken both mean test or examination. Ji is any character or letter, while kanji is specifically a Chinese character. This ji is not the ji in ichiji (one o'clock), which is a different word that happens to sound the same.

Adverbs for adjectives

These four words go right before an adjective and change how strong it is.

KanaRomajiEnglish
ちょっとchottoa little
とてもtotemovery
たいへんtaihenvery
あまり(~ない)amari (~nai)not very

Totemo and taihen are used the same way. Amari always needs a negative ending, so say amari takakunai desu, never amari takai desu.

PatternExampleMeaning
chotto + adjectiveちょっと ふるいですa little old
totemo + adjectiveとても たかいですvery expensive
taihen + adjectiveたいへん いそがしいですvery busy
amari + negativeあまり ひまじゃありませんnot very free

Adjective pairs

The book teaches these as 21 pairs of opposites. Learn each pair together: when you remember one side, the other comes free. The Types column shows whether each word is an い-adjective or a な-adjective, which decides how it conjugates.

AdjectiveOppositeTypes
ながい (nagai) longみじかい (mijikai) shortい + い
ちかい (chikai) nearとおい (tooi) farい + い
つよい (tsuyoi) strongよわい (yowai) weakい + い
かんたん(な) (kantan(na)) easyむずかしい (muzukashii) difficultな + い
おおきい (ookii) bigちいさい (chiisai) smallい + い
おもい (omoi) heavyかるい (karui) lightい + い
おもしろい (omoshiroi) interesting, funnyつまらない (tsumaranai) boringい + い
ひろい (hiroi) wideせまい (semai) narrowい + い
きれい(な) (kirei(na)) clean, beautifulきたない (kitanai) dirtyな + い
あたらしい (atarashii) newふるい (furui) oldい + い
あかるい (akarui) brightくらい (kurai) darkい + い
しずか(な) (shizuka(na)) silentにぎやか(な) (nigiyaka(na)) livelyな + な
たかい (takai) expensiveやすい (yasui) cheapい + い
たかい (takai) high, tallひくい (hikui) lowい + い
ひま(な) (hima(na)) freeいそがしい (isogashii) busyな + い
べんり(な) (benri(na)) convenientふべん(な) (fuben(na)) inconvenientな + な
いい・よい (ii / yoi) goodわるい (warui) badい + い
あつい (atsui) hot (things)つめたい (tsumetai) cold (things)い + い
あつい (atsui) hot (weather)さむい (samui) cold (weather)い + い
あつい (atsui) thickうすい (usui) thinい + い
おいしい (oishii) deliciousまずい (mazui) bad tasteい + い

The (な) after a word, as in きれい(な), marks a な-adjective. The な only shows up when the adjective sits in front of a noun. いい (good) is the one adjective that cannot be conjugated, so よい takes over: よくない (not good) and よかった (was good).

More adjectives

The grammar page that opens the chapter gives three example words of each type. They are not in the pairs table, so learn them separately.

KanaRomajiEnglishType
たのしいtanoshiienjoyableい-adjective
あぶないabunaidangerousい-adjective
やさしいyasashiikind, easyい-adjective
いろいろ(な)iroiro(na)variousな-adjective
りっぱ(な)rippa(na)splendidな-adjective
ゆうめい(な)yuumei(na)famousな-adjective

One word, several meanings

The meaning comes from what the word describes.

WordMeaningExample from the book
たかい (takai)expensiveたかい じてんしゃ (expensive bicycle)
たかい (takai)high, tallたかい たてもの (tall building)
あつい (atsui)hot (things)あつい コーヒー (hot coffee)
あつい (atsui)hot (weather)きょうは あついです (it is hot today)
あつい (atsui)thickあつい おもい ほん (thick, heavy book)
やさしい (yasashii)kind, easyやさしい せんせい (kind teacher)

In kanji the three atsui words are written differently, so the kanji will tell them apart later.

Easy to mix up

  • きれい and ゆうめい end in い but are な-adjectives. Say きれいな へや (clean room) and ゆうめいな こうえん (famous park), and きれいじゃありません for the negative.
  • たのしい and おもしろい are close. In the book, たのしい describes a party, a job and Japanese study, while おもしろい describes a book and a movie.
  • わるい means bad in general, while まずい only means bad taste. かんたん (a な-adjective) and やさしい (an い-adjective) can both mean easy, but only やさしい also means kind.

Words from the lessons and exercises

These are not in the chapter's vocabulary list, but you need them to follow the examples, the review exercises and the reading about Japan's seasons.

KanaRomajiEnglishWhere it appears

コーヒーko-hi-coffee6.3 example (delicious and hot coffee)

はなみhanamiflower viewingReview IV reading, spring
はなびhanabifireworksReview IV reading, summer
はなびたいかいhanabi taikaifireworks displayReview IV reading, summer

Hanami is the flower plus looking, and hanabi is the flower plus fire. Taikai also showed up in supo-tsu taikai (sports festival) in Chapter 4.

The reading also uses the seasons, which you met in Chapter 4.

KanaRomajiEnglish
はるharuspring
なつnatsusummer
あきakiautumn
ふゆfuyuwinter
きせつkisetsuseason

docs.title: Intensive Japanese 1 Chapter 7 Reviewer
docs.intro: Chapter 7 is about daily routines: when you wake up, work, rest and sleep. This reviewer covers the grammar, every word, the mix-ups to watch for, and a self-test. The exercise answers are in the separate answer key.
docs.html:
Chapter 7 is about daily routines: when you wake up, work, rest and sleep. This reviewer covers the grammar, every word, the mix-ups to watch for, and a self-test. The exercise answers are in the separate answer key.

How to use this reviewer

  • Read each grammar table, then say the examples out loud with the English covered.
  • Learn the vocabulary the same way: cover one column and say the other.
  • Read the mix-ups section before the self-test. It covers the mistakes the exercises are built around.
  • Finish with the self-test and check yourself against its key.

Grammar: verb endings and time markers

This is the first chapter with verbs. The book uses the formal form, which adds an ending to the verb. The dictionary form comes later, in Chapter 9.

FormEndingExampleMeaning
Present positive~ますねますsleep, will sleep
Present negative~ませんねませんdo not sleep, will not sleep
Past positive~ましたねましたslept
Past negative~ませんでしたねませんでしたdid not sleep

The present form also covers the future, so らいげつ おわります means finishes next month. Words like べんきょう, しごと, ざんぎょう and きゅうけい become verbs by adding します, and only the します part changes: べんきょうしません, べんきょうしました, べんきょうしませんでした.

Time markers

PatternMeaningExampleMeaning
time + に + verbon, atごじはんに おきますwake up at 5:30
time + から + verbfromさんじから きゅうけいしますtake a break from 3 o'clock
time + まで + verbuntilくじはんまで きゅうけいしましたtook a break until 9:30
time + ごろ + verbaroundしちじはんごろ おきますwake up around 7:30
span of time + で + verbwithin, inさんじゅっぷんで おわりますfinish within 30 minutes
あと + span of time + で + verbafterあと じゅうごふんで きゅうけいしますtake a break after 15 minutes
  • に goes after a specific time: a clock time, a day of the week, a month or a date, as in ごじはんに, どようびに, じゅうにがつに.
  • Time words that are not specific take no に: きのう, あした, あさって, ゆうべ, こんばん, まいにち, せんしゅう, らいげつ.
  • から, まで and ごろ sit straight after the time with no に added.
  • ごろ gives a time around a point (しちじはんごろ). ぐらい from Chapter 5 gives an amount of time (よじかん ぐらい かかります).

Grammar: adjectives as adverbs and how often

An adjective can describe how an action is done. Put it right before the verb and change its ending.

TypeHow it changesExampleMeaning
い-adjectivedrop い, add くはやい → はやく おきますwake up early
い-adjectivedrop い, add くおそい → おそく おわりますfinish late
い-adjectiveいい uses よい, then くよい → よく ねましたslept well
な-adjectivedrop な, add にしずか(な) → しずかに きゅうけいしますtake a break quietly
な-adjectivedrop な, add にまじめ(な) → まじめに べんきょうしましたstudied seriously
な-adjectivedrop な, add にげんき(な) → げんきに おきましたwoke up in good health

Do not use くて here. くて joins two adjectives, as in Chapter 6. Before a verb you want plain く.

How often

WordMeaningExampleMeaning
いつもalwaysいつも ろくじに おきますalways wake up at 6
ときどきsometimesときどき にちようびに しごとしますsometimes work on Sunday
ぜんぜん(~ない)never, not at allごじはんに ぜんぜん おきませんnever wake up at 5:30

ぜんぜん always needs a negative ending, just like あまり from Chapter 6. あまり means not very, while ぜんぜん means not at all.

Vocabulary

The book's vocabulary list for this chapter has 29 words: 11 verbs, 8 nouns, 7 adjectives and 3 how-often words. The extra words that the lessons and exercises use come last.

Verbs

KanaRomajiEnglish
おきますokimasuwake up
ねますnemasusleep
やすみますyasumimasurest
はじまりますhajimarimasustart
おわりますowarimasufinish
はたらきますhatarakimasuwork
しごとしますshigotoshimasuwork
ざんぎょうしますzangyoushimasuwork overtime
べんきょうしますbenkyoushimasustudy
きゅうけいしますkyuukeishimasutake a break
うまれますumaremasube born

The book gives these in the polite ~ます form only for now. おきます and ねます are an opposite pair, and so are はじまります and おわります. はたらきます and しごとします both mean work, but しごとします is just しごと (work) plus します.

Nouns

KanaRomajiEnglish
くすりkusurimedicine
プレゼントpurezentopresent, gift
メールme-ruemail
レポートrepo-toreport
クレジットカードkurejitto ka-docredit card
えいがeigamovie
いしゃishadoctor
しんにゅうしゃいんshinnyuushainnew employee

Adjectives

KanaRomajiEnglish
はやいhayaiearly, fast
おそいosoilate, slow
きびしいkibishiistrict
あぶないabunaidangerous
ねむいnemuisleepy
まじめ(な)majime(na)serious, industrious
げんき(な)genki(na)fine, healthy

まじめ and げんき are な-adjectives. The other five are い-adjectives, and あぶない is the same word as in Chapter 6. はやい and おそい are opposites, and each has two meanings, so the sentence tells you which one is meant. ねむい (sleepy) shares its root with ねます (sleep).

How often

KanaRomajiEnglish
いつもitsumoalways
ときどきtokidokisometimes
ぜんぜん(~ない)zenzen (~nai)never, not at all

Extra words from the lessons and exercises

KanaRomajiEnglishWhere it appears
ひるやすみhiruyasumilunch breakReview III reading
あとatoafter7.5 examples
いっかげつikkagetsuone month (same as ひとつき)7.5 and the exercises
いっしゅうかんisshuukanone weekchoose the marker exercise
にかいnikaitwicechoose the marker exercise
なんかいnankaihow many timesReview V, question 10

Time words from Chapter 4 that you need

KanaRomajiEnglish
あさasamorning
ひるhirunoon, daytime
よるyorunight
けさkesathis morning
まいあさmaiasaevery morning
ゆうべyuubelast night
こんばんkonbantonight
まいばんmaibanevery night
おとといototoithe day before yesterday
あさってasattethe day after tomorrow

Easy to mix up

These are the mistakes the Chapter 7 exercises keep testing.

Mix-upThe ruleExample
に or no にA specific time takes に. Relative time words take none. Quick test: if the word could answer なんじ, なんようび or なんがつ, use に.ろくじに おきます and あした おきます
ごろ or ぐらいごろ is around a point in time. ぐらい is about how long.ろくじごろ おきます and よじかん ぐらい かかります
から, まで or でから is the start, まで is the end, and で is within a span of time.くじから じゅうじまで きゅうけいします and いちじかんで おわります
じ or じかん~じ is a clock time and ~じかん is a length of time. なんじに asks when, なんじかん asks how long.じゅうじはんに ねます (at 10:30) and じゅうじかん ねます (for 10 hours)
く or にAn い-adjective ends in く before a verb, and a な-adjective takes に. Before a noun, a な-adjective takes な.はやく おきます, しずかに べんきょうします, しずかな がくせい
ません or ませんでしたMatch the tense to the time word. きのう, ゆうべ, けさ and せんしゅう are past, so use ~ました or ~ませんでした.せんしゅう ぜんぜん はたらきませんでした
ぜんぜんIt always needs a negative ending, in the present or the past.ぜんぜん ねません
How oftenA span of time plus に, then the number of times, says how often.いっしゅうかんに にかい やすみます (rest twice a week)

Self-test

Part A: What does it mean?

These are the answers to all 86 exercise items in the Chapter 7 workbook, in page order. Review V asks about you, so it gives sample answers you can swap for your own.

Verb conjugation (page 103)

Drop ます and add ません, ました or ませんでした. The first row, おきます, was already done in the book.

Present positivePresent negativePast positivePast negative
はじまりますはじまりませんはじまりましたはじまりませんでした
はたらきますはたらきませんはたらきましたはたらきませんでした
きゅうけいしますきゅうけいしませんきゅうけいしましたきゅうけいしませんでした
おわりますおわりませんおわりましたおわりませんでした
しごとしますしごとしませんしごとしましたしごとしませんでした
ざんぎょうしますざんぎょうしませんざんぎょうしましたざんぎょうしませんでした
やすみますやすみませんやすみましたやすみませんでした

Change to negative (page 105)

Keep the tense. Items 1, 5, 7 and 10 are already past, so they end in ませんでした. The rest end in ません.

#AnswerMeaning
1けさ ろくじに おきませんでした。I did not wake up at 6 this morning.
2とおかに やすみません。I will not rest on the 10th.
3げつようびに しごとしません。I will not work on Monday.
4しがつに おわりません。It will not finish in April.
5じゅうにじに ねませんでした。I did not sleep at 12.
6まいにち ざんぎょうしません。I do not work overtime every day.
7さんじに きゅうけいしませんでした。I did not take a break at 3.
8こんしゅう はたらきません。I will not work this week.
9こんばん べんきょうしません。I will not study tonight.
10ごがつふつかに はじまりませんでした。It did not start on May 2nd.

Change to past tense (page 105)

Positive verbs end in ました. Items 4 and 8 are negative, so they become ませんでした.

#AnswerMeaning
1しちじに おきました。I woke up at 7.
2きんようびに おわりました。It finished on Friday.
3ごがつに はじまりました。It started in May.
4じゅうにじはんに ねませんでした。I did not sleep at 12:30.
5すいようびに べんきょうしました。I studied on Wednesday.
6くじごふんに きゅうけいしました。I took a break at 9:05.
7とおかに はたらきました。I worked on the 10th.
8どようびに ざんぎょうしませんでした。I did not work overtime on Saturday.
9かようびに しごとしました。I worked on Tuesday.
10いちがつに やすみました。I rested in January.

Choose between 1 and 2 (page 107)

A clock time or a day of the week takes に. Relative words like あした, ゆうべ and まいにち do not. Item 5 is a ごろ or ぐらい choice, and ごろ is for a time of day.

#AnswerFull sentenceMeaning
12 さんじにかいぎは さんじに はじまります。The meeting starts at 3.
22 きんようびにじゅぎょうは きんようびに おわります。The class ends on Friday.
32 なんじにこんばん なんじに ねますか。What time will you sleep tonight?
41 あしたあした はたらきます。I will work tomorrow.
51 ろくじごろまいあさ ろくじごろ おきます。I wake up around 6 every morning.
61 ゆうべゆうべ ざんぎょうしました。I worked overtime last night.
71 まいにちまいにち べんきょうします。I study every day.
82 はちじからはちじから しごとします。I work from 8 o'clock.
92 かようびにらいしゅうの かようびに やすみますか。Will you rest on Tuesday next week?
101 こんばんこんばん おわりますか。Does it finish tonight?

Choose the adverb or marker (page 110)

#AnswerFull sentenceWhy
12 はやくげつようびから きんようびまで はやく おきます。An い-adjective takes く before a verb.
23 まじめにおとうとは まじめに べんきょうします。A な-adjective takes に before a verb.
32 でミーティングは いちじかんで はじまります。で after a span of time means within it.
43 からくじはんから じゅうじまで きゅうけいします。から is the start, matching まで for the end.
52 おそくおとといの よる おそく ねました。おそい becomes おそく before a verb.
63 べんきょうしませんでしたきのう ぜんぜん べんきょうしませんでした。ぜんぜん needs a negative, and きのう is past.
72 でにほんごのクラスは いっかげつで おわります。で after a span of time means within it.
83 にいっしゅうかんに にかい べんきょうします。に after a span of time gives how often.

Meanings in order: wake up early Monday to Friday; my younger brother studies seriously; the meeting starts within an hour; take a break from 9:30 until 10; slept late the night before last; did not study at all yesterday; the class finishes within a month; study twice a week.

Review I, choose the grammar pattern (page 111)

#AnswerWhy
11 いつもA asks about every day, and B says yes, always.
24 ろくじかんなんじかん asks how many hours, so the answer is a length of time.
32 はやくAn い-adjective takes く before a verb.
42 じゅうじはんなんじに asks for a clock time, so 10:30.
54 にA な-adjective takes に before a verb.
64 あさっておわります is present or future, so it needs a future time word.
72 はやく ねませんThe question is about every night, so a present negative.
83 はじまりましたせんしゅう is last week, so the verb is past.

Review II, rearrange the words (page 112)

The order column lists which word number goes in blanks 1 to 4. The full sentence is shown too.

#OrderFull sentenceMeaning

34 1 3 2あいみさんの えいごの クラスは きょう おわります。Aimi's English class ends today.
44 1 3 2けさの かいぎは はやく おわりました。This morning's meeting ended early.
54 1 2 3まいばん わたしは おそく ねます。I sleep late every night.

Review III and IV, fill in and reading (pages 113 and 114)

ItemAnswerWhy
III (1)3 いそがしいTraining runs Monday to Friday with a test and a report, so this week is very busy.
III (2)1 おわりますIt is the daily schedule: training starts at 9 and ends at 4.

Review V, answer in sentences (page 115)

These questions are about you, so there is no single right answer. Any reply works if it answers the question word the right way and the verb tense matches. なんじに gets a time with に, なんじごろ gets a time with ごろ, なんじかん gets a length of time, and なんかい gets a number of times.

#Sample answerAnother way to answer
1まいあさ ろくじごろ おきます。まいあさ しちじごろ おきます。
2けさ ろくじはんに おきました。けさ しちじに おきました。
3ゆうべ じゅうにじに ねました。ゆうべ じゅうじに ねました。
4まいばん じゅうじごろ ねます。まいばん じゅういちじごろ ねます。
5せんしゅう はじまりました。ごがつに はじまりました。
6らいげつ おわります。じゅうにがつに おわります。
7まいばん ななじかん ねます。まいばん ろくじかん ねます。
8まいにち はちじかん はたらきます。まいにち にじかん べんきょうします。
9まいしゅう じゅうじかんぐらい べんきょうします。まいしゅう ごじかんぐらい べんきょうします。
10いっしゅうかんに いっかい やすみます。いっしゅうかんに にかい やすみます。

Review VI, translate to Japanese (page 115)

#JapaneseNote
1まいあさ ろくじに おきます。に goes after the clock time.
2まいにち べんきょうします。まいにち takes no に.
3いちじかんで おわります。で after a span of time means within it.
4いつも はやく おきます。いつも goes before the verb, and はやい becomes はやく.
5にほんごの クラスは らいげつ おわります。らいげつ takes no に.
6ゆうべ ざんぎょうしましたか。A past question, and ゆうべ takes no に.
7ゆうべ なんじごろ ねましたか。なんじごろ asks around what time.
8にほんごの トレーニングは らいしゅう はじまります。らいしゅう takes no に.
9ときどき ざんぎょうしますか。ときどき goes before the verb.
10くじはんに ちょっと きゅうけいしました。ちょっと (a little) from Chapter 6 gives the short break.

Meanings in order: every morning I wake up at 6; I study every day; I will finish in one hour; I always wake up early; my Japanese class ends next month; did you work overtime last night; around what time did you sleep last night; the Japanese training starts next week; do you sometimes work overtime; I took a short break at 9:30.

docs.intro: Chapter 8 teaches you how to say what you do to something: eat it, drink it, read it, write it, buy it. You also learn the small markers that say where, with whom, to whom and how. Everything here comes from pages 115 to 129 of the workbook.
docs.html:
Chapter 8 teaches you how to say what you do to something: eat it, drink it, read it, write it, buy it. You also learn the small markers that say where, with whom, to whom and how. Everything here comes from pages 115 to 129 of the workbook.

How to use this reviewer

  • Read the grammar once, then cover the English column and try to say each sentence out loud.
  • Learn the vocabulary in the order it appears: food, drinks, reading, then the verbs.
  • Skim the mix-ups before the self-test, then do the self-test without peeking at the key.

Grammar: the patterns Chapter 8 teaches, with examples

A transitive verb is a verb that acts on something (eat bread, read a book). In Japanese the verb always comes last, and the small marker after each word tells you what job that word does. All the verbs here are in the formal ます forms from Chapter 7.

The markers at a glance

MarkerJobQuestion wordExample
をthe thing the action is done to (object)なにを (what)パンを たべます。
でwhere the action happens (at, in)どこで (where)きっさてんで のみます。
にwho receives the action (to, for)だれに / どなたに (to or for whom)せんせいに ききます。
とwho does it with you (with)だれと / どなたと (with whom)ともだちと みます。
でhow you do it: method or language (in, by)なにで / どうやって (how)えいごで はなします。
でwhat you use: the tool (with, using)なにで (what tool, how)はしで たべます。

8.1 A は Object を Transitive Verb

Say who does what to what: A (verb) an object.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
アナさんは とけいを かいます。Ana-san wa tokei o kaimasu.Ana will buy a watch.
ジョンさんは 本を よみます。Jon-san wa hon o yomimasu.John reads a book.
かちょうは メールを かきます。kachou wa me-ru o kakimasu.The section chief writes an email.
あには コーヒーを のみました。ani wa ko-hi- o nomimashita.My older brother drank coffee.
わたしは えいごを おしえました。watashi wa eigo o oshiemashita.I taught English.
おとうとは おんがくを ききます。otouto wa ongaku o kikimasu.My younger brother listens to music.
わたしは しょうせつを よみません。watashi wa shousetsu o yomimasen.I don't read novels.
キムさんは でんわを かけませんでした。Kimu-san wa denwa o kakemasen deshita.Kim did not make a phone call.

The verb changes its ending to show positive or negative, and present or past:

VerbPresent positivePresent negativePast positivePast negative
eatたべますたべませんたべましたたべませんでした
smokeすいますすいませんすいましたすいませんでした
call (a phone)かけますかけませんかけましたかけませんでした
  • Endings in romaji: -masu, -masen, -mashita, -masen deshita. Every verb in this chapter follows the same four endings.
  • The present form covers both a habit (I eat breakfast every day) and the future (I will buy a watch).
  • In a negative sentence, the object marker を can change into は to put the spotlight on that thing: しょうせつは よみません means that novels are the thing you don't read.

8.2 Time expression に・から・まで・ごろ + Transitive Verb

Time words from Chapter 7 slot in before the object. The marker に is used only with a specific time, such as a clock time or a day of the week. It is not used with non-specific time words like 毎朝, けさ, 毎晩 or まいしゅう.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
毎朝 あさごはんを たべます。maiasa asagohan o tabemasu.I eat breakfast every morning.
いとうせんせいは 三時から おしえます。Itou-sensei wa san-ji kara oshiemasu.Mr. Ito teaches from three o'clock.
よる 八時ごろ ニュースを みます。yoru hachi-ji goro nyu-su o mimasu.I watch the news at around eight in the evening.
まいしゅう かいしゃの レポートを かきます。maishuu kaisha no re-po-to o kakimasu.I write the company report every week.
日よう日に あたらしい くつを かいました。nichiyoubi ni atarashii kutsu o kaimashita.I bought new shoes on Sunday.
けさ ぎゅうにゅうを のみました。kesa gyuunyuu o nomimashita.I drank milk this morning.
毎晩 しょうせつを よみます。maiban shousetsu o yomimasu.I read a novel every night.
金よう日まで くすりを のみます。kinyoubi made kusuri o nomimasu.I take medicine until Friday.

8.3 Place of action で

Place + で + verb: the place where the action happens (at, in).

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
きっさてんで コーヒーを のみます。kissaten de ko-hi- o nomimasu.I drink coffee at the coffee shop.
としょかんで べんきょうしました。toshokan de benkyou shimashita.I studied at the library.
大学で おしえます。daigaku de oshiemasu.I teach at the university.
カラオケで うたいました。karaoke de utaimashita.I sang at karaoke.
しょくどうで たべます。shokudou de tabemasu.I eat at the cafeteria.
えいがかんで えいがを みました。eigakan de eiga o mimashita.I watched a movie at the movie theater.
デパートで かいました。depa-to de kaimashita.I bought it at the department store.
日本で はたらきます。nihon de hatarakimasu.I work in Japan.

8.4 Recipient of action に

Person + に + verb: the person who receives the action (to, for).

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
アナさんに でんわを かけます。Ana-san ni denwa o kakemasu.I will call Ana.
たなかさんに てがみを かきました。Tanaka-san ni tegami o kakimashita.I wrote a letter to Mr. Tanaka.
せんせいに ききました。sensei ni kikimashita.I asked the teacher.
あにに とけいを かいます。ani ni tokei o kaimasu.I will buy a watch for my older brother.
おかあさんに はなしました。okaasan ni hanashimashita.I talked to my mother.
こどもに 本を よみます。kodomo ni hon o yomimasu.I read a book to the child.

8.5 Companion と・といっしょに

Person + と (or と いっしょに) + verb: the person who does it together with you (with). いっしょに just stresses the word together.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
しゃちょうと はなしました。shachou to hanashimashita.I talked with the company president.
ともだちと おんがくを ききます。tomodachi to ongaku o kikimasu.I listen to music with friends.
あねと いっしょに えいがを みました。ane to issho ni eiga o mimashita.I watched a movie with my older sister.
かぞくと ばんごはんを たべました。kazoku to bangohan o tabemashita.I ate dinner with my family.
キムさんと コーラを かいます。Kimu-san to ko-ra o kaimasu.I will buy cola with Kim.
ベンさんと コーヒーを のみます。Ben-san to ko-hi- o nomimasu.I will drink coffee with Ben.

The book's English line for the Kim example says cellphone, but コーラ is cola.

8.6 Method of action で

Method + で + verb: how you do the action. Language words land here too (in Korean, in English, in Japanese).

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
ともだちと かんこくごで はなしました。tomodachi to kankokugo de hanashimashita.I spoke with my friends in Korean.
学生に えいごで おしえます。gakusei ni eigo de oshiemasu.I teach the students in English.
日本語で レポートを かきました。nihongo de re-po-to o kakimashita.I wrote the report in Japanese.

8.7 Tool of action で

Tool + で + verb: the thing you use to do the action (with, using).

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
はしで ラーメンを たべます。hashi de ra-men o tabemasu.I eat ramen with chopsticks.
えんぴつで てがみを かきます。enpitsu de tegami o kakimasu.I write letters with a pencil.
スプーンで スープを のみます。supu-n de su-pu o nomimasu.I drink soup with a spoon.

Asking with question words

The question word takes the same marker its answer will take. Swap the question word for the real answer and the marker stays put.

QuestionAnswerEnglish
けさ なにを たべましたか。けさ パンを たべました。What did you eat this morning? I ate bread.
だれに メールを かきましたか。かちょうに メールを かきました。Who did you write the email to? I wrote it to the section chief.
ラーメンを なにで たべますか。はしで たべます。What do you eat ramen with? I eat it with chopsticks.
それを どこで かいましたか。ほんやで かいました。Where did you buy that? I bought it at the bookstore.
だれと えいがを みますか。アナさんと えいがを みます。Who will you watch a movie with? I will watch with Ana.
どうやって おしえますか。えいごで おしえます。How do you teach? I teach in English.
なにを よみますか。しょうせつを よみます。What do you read? I read novels.

More sample sentences

These mix several markers in one sentence. Try spotting each marker and its job.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
らいしゅうの 日よう日に ともだちと えいがを みます。raishuu no nichiyoubi ni tomodachi to eiga o mimasu.I will watch a movie with a friend next Sunday.
ゆうべ ははに でんわを かけました。yuube haha ni denwa o kakemashita.I called my mother last night.
いっしゅうかんに いっかい かいしゃの レポートを かきます。isshuukan ni ikkai kaisha no re-po-to o kakimasu.I write the company report once a week.
先生と きょうしつで じゅうごふん はなしました。sensei to kyoushitsu de juugofun hanashimashita.I talked with the teacher in the classroom for fifteen minutes.
毎日 かぞくと ばんごはんを たべます。mainichi kazoku to bangohan o tabemasu.I eat dinner with my family every day.
日本で 一年間 べんきょうしました。nihon de ichinenkan benkyou shimashita.I studied in Japan for one year.
やまださんは モールで あたらしい カメラを かいました。Yamada-san wa mo-ru de atarashii kamera o kaimashita.Mr. Yamada bought a new camera at the mall.
先生は 日本語で おしえます。sensei wa nihongo de oshiemasu.The teacher teaches in Japanese.
おとうとは いつも へやで おんがくを ききます。otouto wa itsumo heya de ongaku o kikimasu.My younger brother always listens to music in his room.

Two patterns hide in here. A length of time (一年間, じゅうごふん) takes no marker at all. And いっしゅうかんに いっかい uses に to mean per, so it reads once per week.

Phrases from the conversations

The five short conversations on page 124 give you handy real-life lines.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
毎日 レポートを かきますか。mainichi re-po-to o kakimasu ka.Do you write a report every day?
ちょっと、むずかしいです。chotto, muzukashii desu.It is a little difficult.
日本語が じょうずですね。nihongo ga jouzu desu ne.You are good at Japanese.
いいえ、まだまだです。iie, madamada desu.No, not yet. (a modest reply to a compliment)
どのぐらいですか。donogurai desu ka.About how long?
十か月ぐらいです。jukkagetsu gurai desu.About ten months.
にほんごの べんきょうは どうでしたか。nihongo no benkyou wa dou deshita ka.How was your Japanese study?
おもしろかったです。omoshirokatta desu.It was interesting.
ゆうべ 何時ごろ ねましたか。yuube nanji goro nemashita ka.About what time did you go to bed last night?
九時ごろです。kuji goro desu.Around nine o'clock.
いくらぐらい ですか。ikura gurai desu ka.About how much is it?
十万円ぐらいです。juuman en gurai desu.About 100,000 yen.
パンと くだものです。pan to kudamono desu.Bread and fruit.
ぎゅうにゅうは のみません。gyuunyuu wa nomimasen.I don't drink milk. (other drinks, yes)

Vocabulary: every Chapter 8 word with romaji and English

The workbook gives you 31 nouns and 13 verbs (pages 116 to 118). The nouns come in themed groups, so learn them one small group at a time. The meal words follow a pattern: あさ (morning), ひる (noon) or ばん (evening) plus ごはん.

Food (たべもの)

Other nouns

KanaRomajiEnglish
スプーンsupu-nspoon

Verbs (どうしリスト)

KanaRomajiEnglish
たべますtabemasueat
のみますnomimasudrink

(でんわを) かけます(denwa o) kakemasucall (a phone)

The verbs on this list are in the formal ます form. The dictionary form, the one you look up in a dictionary, comes later in Chapter 9.

Which verb goes with which noun

Learning words in pairs helps a lot. Most nouns above only fit one or two verbs.

VerbOften paired withExample
たべますあさごはん, ひるごはん, ばんごはん, ごはん, ラーメン, パンパンを たべます。 (I eat bread.)
のみますみず, おちゃ, こうちゃ, ぎゅうにゅう, コーヒー, コーラ, ジュース, おさけ, ビール, ワイン, スープ, くすりビールを のみます。 (I drink beer.)
よみますしょうせつ, ざっし, しんぶん, 本ざっしを よみます。 (I read a magazine.)
ききますおんがく, うた (to listen), or a person plus に (to ask)おんがくを ききます。 (I listen to music.)
みますニュース, えいが, テレビニュースを みます。 (I watch the news.)
