Easy to mix up

These are the spots where Chapter 8 trips most people up. Each row gives you a quick test you can run in your head.

Markers that look alike

Mix-upQuick testExample
で (place) vs に (being somewhere)で goes with an action verb. に goes with います or あります.かいしゃで はたらきます (I work at the company) vs かいしゃに います (I am at the company)
に (recipient) vs と (companion)Does the other person do the action too? If they join you, use と. If they only receive it, use に.ともだちに でんわを かけます (I call a friend) vs ともだちと えいがを みます (I watch a movie with a friend)
と (with) vs と (and)と after a person, right before the verb, means with. と between two nouns means and.かぞくと たべます (I eat with my family) vs パンと くだもの (bread and fruit)
で as place, method or toolAsk the question. どこで means place, どうやって means method, なにで means tool.としょかんで (at the library), えいごで (in English), はしで (with chopsticks)
を vs は in a negative sentenceを is neutral. は puts the spotlight on the thing you do not do.ビールを のみます。ワインは のみません。 (I drink beer, but not wine.)
に with time wordsUse に with a clock time or a day of the week. Leave it out with けさ, 毎朝, 毎晩, まいしゅう and いつも.日よう日に かいました (bought it on Sunday) vs けさ のみました (drank it this morning)

Verbs that look or sound alike

GroupHow to keep them straight
かきます / かいます / かけますOne sound apart. かき is write, かい is buy, かけ is call (a phone).
みます / のみます / よみますAll end in -mimasu. み alone is watch or see, のみ is drink, よみ is read.
ききます / かきますOnly the first sound changes. きき is listen or ask, かき is write.
うります / うたいますBoth start with う. うり is sell, うたい is sing.
かいます / うりますOpposites. かいます is buy, うります is sell.

One verb, two meanings

VerbMeaning depends on the markerExample
ききますを after the thing means listen. に after a person means ask.おんがくを ききます (I listen to music) vs せんせいに ききます (I ask the teacher)
はなしますと means talk with someone. に means talk to someone. で after a language means speak in it.しゃちょうと はなします vs おかあさんに はなします vs えいごで はなします
みますOne verb covers watch, look and see.えいがを みます (I watch a movie)

Little words that travel together

PairRuleExample
ぜんぜん + negativeぜんぜん always goes with a negative ending, never with ます.ぜんぜん のみません (I never drink it)
ときどき, いつも, 毎日 + positiveThese go with ます or ました.ときどき のみます (I drink it sometimes)
ごろ vs ぐらいごろ is around a point in time. ぐらい is about an amount of time, money or distance.九時ごろ (around nine o'clock) vs 二時間ぐらい (about two hours), 十万円ぐらい (about 100,000 yen)
から / まで vs にから is the start, まで is the end, に is one exact point.三時から 六時まで (from three to six) vs 三時に (at three)
a length of timeA length of time takes no marker.一年間 べんきょうしました (I studied for a year)
おととい and ゆうべBoth point to the past, so the verb ends in ました.おととい でんわを かけました (I called the day before yesterday)

Food and drink look-alikes

PairDifference
おちゃ / こうちゃおちゃ is tea, こうちゃ is black tea.
ごはん / あさごはんごはん is a meal or cooked rice. Add あさ, ひる or ばん to say which meal.
おさけ / ビール / ワインおさけ is liquor in general. ビール and ワイン are two kinds of it.
うた / うたいますうた is a song and うたいます is to sing. You sing a song: うたを うたいます.
しょうせつ / ざっし / しんぶんNovel, magazine and newspaper. All three are よみもの, so all three go with よみます.

These ask about you, so the answers below are samples. Each one shows the pattern the question is drilling. Any true answer in a full sentence works.

#QuestionSample answerMeaning
1しょうせつを よみますか。どんな しょうせつ ですか。はい、よみます。おもしろい しょうせつです。Yes, I read. They are interesting novels.
2毎朝 あさごはんを たべますか。けさ なにを たべましたか。はい、毎朝 たべます。けさ パンを たべました。Yes, every morning. I ate bread this morning.
3コーヒーを のみますか。まいにち のみますか。はい、のみます。まいにち のみます。Yes, I drink it. I drink it every day.
4あなたのくつは どこで かいましたか。デパートで かいました。I bought them at a department store.
5毎日 どこで ひるごはんを たべますか。毎日 しょくどうで ひるごはんを たべます。I eat lunch at the cafeteria every day.
6日本語を どこで べんきょうしますか。日本語を きょうしつで べんきょうします。I study Japanese in the classroom.
7日本のおんがくを ききますか。どんなおんがくを ききますか。はい、ききます。あたらしい おんがくを ききます。Yes, I listen to it. I listen to new music.
8テレビを みますか。毎日 どのぐらい みますか。はい、みます。毎日 二時間ぐらい みます。Yes, I watch it. About two hours every day.
9うたを うたいますか。どんなうたを うたいますか。はい、うたいます。日本の うたを うたいます。Yes, I sing. I sing Japanese songs.
10日本の りょうりを たべますか。どこで たべますか。はい、たべます。レストランで たべます。Yes, I eat it. I eat at a restaurant.

A negative answer also works. For example, for number 3 you could say いいえ、コーヒーは のみません。 (No, I don't drink coffee.)

#EnglishAnswerNotes
1I listen to Japanese music.日本の おんがくを ききます。を marks what you listen to.
2I will talk with Mr. Tanaka.たなかさんと はなします。と for the companion.
3I will study inside the room.へやで べんきょうします。で for the place.
4I watched a movie with my friend last Saturday.せんしゅうの 土よう日に ともだちと えいがを みました。に after the day of the week, と for the companion, past tense.
5I will call Ana at around 9:30.九時はんごろ アナさんに でんわを かけます。ごろ for around a clock time, に for the person you call.
6Mr. Yamada drinks coffee at the coffee shop.やまださんは きっさてんで コーヒーを のみます。で for the place.
7Mr. Cruz will work in Japan from next month.クルスさんは らいげつから 日本で はたらきます。から for the start, で for the place.
8I write company reports every week.まいしゅう かいしゃの レポートを かきます。No に after まいしゅう.
9Kim will teach Korean language to the students.キムさんは 学生に かんこくごを おしえます。に for the students, を for the subject taught.
10Where did you buy your cell phone?けいたいでんわを どこで かいましたか。どこで asks about the place. ケータイ also works for cell phone.

How to use this reviewer

  • Cover the English column, read the Japanese, and say the meaning out loud.
  • Cover the Japanese columns, read the English, and say the word.

Chapter 6: Adjectives

The book's vocabulary list for this chapter has 24 words: places, home words, study words, and a few more. The adjectives and adverbs that the grammar pages teach follow after them.

Places

KanaRomajiEnglish
ところ・ばしょtokoro / bashoplace
たてもの・ビルtatemono / birubuilding
こうえんkouenpark

くうこうkuukouairport

(お)みせ(o)misestore, shop
くすりやkusuriyadrugstore, pharmacy

くうこう is literally an air harbor: くう is air and こう is harbor, the same harbor as みなと. くすりや is くすり (medicine) plus や (shop), the same や as ほんや (bookstore).

Home and food

KanaRomajiEnglish

トイレ and ベッド come from English, so they are in katakana. りょうり means both the dish itself and the act of cooking.

Study and writing

KanaRomajiEnglish

かんじkanjiChinese character

じ is any character or letter, while かんじ is specifically a Chinese character. This じ is not the じ in いちじ (one o'clock), a different word that happens to sound the same.

Adverbs for adjectives

These four words go right before an adjective and change how strong it is.

KanaRomajiEnglish
ちょっとchottoa little

あまり(～ない)amari (~nai)not very

とても and たいへん work the same way. あまり always needs a negative ending: あまり たかくないです, never あまり たかいです.

Adjective pairs

The book teaches these as 21 pairs of opposites. Learn each pair together: when you remember one side, the other comes free. The Types column shows whether each word is an い-adjective or a な-adjective, which decides how it changes.

AdjectiveOppositeTypes
ながい (nagai) longみじかい (mijikai) shortい + い
ちかい (chikai) nearとおい (tooi) farい + い

かんたん(な) (kantan(na)) easyむずかしい (muzukashii) difficultな + い
おおきい (ookii) bigちいさい (chiisai) smallい + い
おもい (omoi) heavyかるい (karui) lightい + い
おもしろい (omoshiroi) interesting, funnyつまらない (tsumaranai) boringい + い
ひろい (hiroi) wideせまい (semai) narrowい + い
きれい(な) (kirei(na)) clean, beautifulきたない (kitanai) dirtyな + い

あかるい (akarui) brightくらい (kurai) darkい + い
しずか(な) (shizuka(na)) silentにぎやか(な) (nigiyaka(na)) livelyな + な
たかい (takai) expensiveやすい (yasui) cheapい + い
たかい (takai) high, tallひくい (hikui) lowい + い
ひま(な) (hima(na)) freeいそがしい (isogashii) busyな + い
べんり(な) (benri(na)) convenientふべん(な) (fuben(na)) inconvenientな + な
いい・よい (ii / yoi) goodわるい (warui) badい + い
あつい (atsui) hot (things)つめたい (tsumetai) cold (things)い + い
あつい (atsui) hot (weather)さむい (samui) cold (weather)い + い
あつい (atsui) thickうすい (usui) thinい + い
おいしい (oishii) deliciousまずい (mazui) bad tasteい + い

The (な) after a word, as in きれい(な), marks a な-adjective. The な only shows up when the adjective sits in front of a noun. いい (good) is the one adjective that cannot be conjugated, so よい takes over: よくない (not good) and よかった (was good).

More adjectives

The grammar page that opens the chapter gives three example words of each type. They are not in the pairs table, so learn them separately.

One word, several meanings

The meaning comes from what the word describes.

docs.intro: The Kanji Workbook N5 teaches kanji 1 to 30 in three lessons: the numbers 1 to 10, then bigger numbers with the days of the week, then people and money. This reviewer covers all 30 kanji with strokes, meanings and readings, every word the workbook uses, the look-alikes and reading traps, and a self-test. The answers to the workbook's own exercises are in the separate answer key.
docs.html:
The Kanji Workbook N5 teaches kanji 1 to 30 in three lessons: the numbers 1 to 10, then bigger numbers with the days of the week, then people and money. This reviewer covers all 30 kanji with strokes, meanings and readings, every word the workbook uses, the look-alikes and reading traps, and a self-test. The answers to the workbook's own exercises are in the separate answer key.

How to use this reviewer

  • Cover the readings, look at the kanji, and say the reading and the meaning.
  • Write each kanji by hand a few times and check your stroke count against the table.
  • Learn the words in the vocabulary tables, because most readings only make sense inside a word.
  • Finish with the mix-ups and the self-test.

Kanji list

How readings work

Most kanji have two kinds of reading. The workbook calls them the Japanese reading (kun'yomi) and the Chinese reading (on'yomi).

  • The Japanese reading is meaning-based. It is the original Japanese word, and you usually see it when the kanji stands alone or has kana after it, as in 一つ (ひとつ).
  • The Chinese reading is sound-based. You usually see it inside compound words, as in 一月 (いちがつ).
  • Some words have a special reading that follows neither pattern, such as 一日 (ついたち), 二十日 (はつか) and 日本 (にほん). The workbook marks these with a star.
  • A reading in square brackets is listed for completeness, but the workbook gives no example words for it.
  • Strokes are always written from left to right and from top to bottom. The Strokes column shows the number the workbook gives.
  • N5 covers about 100 to 150 kanji, so these 30 are a solid start.

Lesson 1: kanji 1 to 10

二本 (にほん), 二分 (にふん), 九分 (きゅうふん) and 七百 (ななひゃく) stay plain. 一人 (ひとり) and 二人 (ふたり) are special: they use the Japanese counting words and not いちにん or ににん. From three people on, the pattern is regular: 三人 (さんにん), but 四人 is よにん and not しにん.

Easy to mix up

Most kanji mistakes come from two places: kanji that look alike, and readings that change from word to word. Skim both tables before any quiz.

Look-alike kanji

Look-alikesHow to tell them apart
日 月 目 白日 (sun, day) is a short box with one bar in the middle. 月 (moon, month) is taller and narrower, with two bars and a hook that curves to the left. 目 (eye) is a straight-sided box with two bars. 白 (white) is 日 with a small slash on top.
白 百百 (hundred) is 白 with a bar added on top.
木 本 休木 (tree) with a bar near the bottom becomes 本 (origin, book). 休, as in 休日 (holiday), is a person 人 leaning on a tree 木.
木 水 火木 has a straight vertical stroke. 水 has a hooked vertical stroke with a splash on each side. 火 looks like a flame with a spark on each side.
人 八人 (person) has its two legs joined at the top. 八 (eight) is two separate strokes that never touch.
七 十七 (seven) is like a 十 whose vertical stroke bends to the right at the bottom. 十 (ten) is a plain cross.
十 千 土 士十 is a plain cross. 千 (thousand) is a 十 with a slanted hat on top. 土 (earth) has two bars, and the lower one is longer. 士 is the opposite, with the upper bar longer. It showed up as a wrong choice in the workbook.
子 字 学 好子 (child) is the base. 字 is 子 under a roof. 学 is 子 under a small crown and a roof. 好 is 女 next to 子. All three of these were wrong choices for こども in the workbook.
母 毎 女母 (mother) is 女 with two dots inside. 毎 (every, as in 毎月) is the same shape with a small hat on top.
男 田 力男 (man) is 田 (rice field) sitting on top of 力 (power).
友 反 刀In 友 (friend), the slanting stroke at the start cuts through the top bar. In 反, that stroke hangs from the end of the bar instead. 刀 (sword) is a different, simpler shape. 反 and 刀 were both wrong choices in the workbook.
四 西 酒 兄四 (four) is a box with two short legs inside. 西 (west) is a lid over a box. 酒 (sake) has the water mark on its left side. 兄 (older brother) is a mouth 口 on top of a person. Only 四 belongs to this workbook.

Reading traps

KanjiWatch out forWhat to remember
一日ついたち or いちにちついたち is the 1st of the month. いちにち is one whole day.
二十日はつか or はたちはつか is the 20th day. はたち is age 20, not a date.
日Lots of readingsひ (sun, day), び (weekday names), にち (にちようび, 十一にち), か (the ending of ふつか, みっか and the rest up to とおか), じつ (きゅうじつ), に (にほん).
日 火Both are read ひ日 is sun or day, 火 is fire. In the weekdays, 日よう日 is にちようび and 火よう日 is かようび.
四し, よん, よよん is the plain number. よ appears in よにん and よっつ. し appears in しがつ.
七しち or ななしち in しちがつ and しちじ. なな in ななつ and ななひゃく. 七日 is なのか.
九く or きゅうく in くがつ and くじ. きゅう in きゅうじゅうきゅう and きゅうふん. 九日 is ここのか and 九つ is ここのつ.
十じゅう, じゅっ, とおじゅう is the plain number. じゅっ comes before さい and ぷん. とお is ten pieces, and 十日 is とおか.
月がつ, かげつ, つき, げつがつ for month names (しがつ). かげつ for how many months (さんかげつ). つき on its own (まいつき). げつ in げつようび and こんげつ.
人ひと, り, にん, じんひとり and ふたり are the only two with り. From three on it is にん, except よにん (not よんにん). People of a nation use じん, like にほんじん.
何人なんにん or なにじんなんにん asks how many people. なにじん asks what nationality. Same kanji, different question.
何なに or なんなに on its own or before か (なにか). なん before です or a counter like 本 or 人 (なんですか, なんぼん).
日本 二本Both can be にほん日本 is Japan (にほん or にっぽん). 二本 is two long objects. The kanji tells you which one.
本ほん, ぽん, ぼんぽん after 1, 6, 8, 10 and 100. ぼん after 3 and 何. ほん after 2, 4, 5, 7 and 9.
千 百Sounds changeさんぜん, はっせん, さんびゃく, ろっぴゃく, はっぴゃく. See the sound-change table above.
父 母ちち, はは or おとうさん, おかあさんちち and はは are for your own parents when talking to other people. おとうさん and おかあさん are for someone else's parents, and for talking to your own parents.
子こ or しこ in こども and おとこのこ. し in だんし and じょし.
金きん or かねきん in きんようび and gold. かね in おかね (money).
男 女Small んおとこ has no ん. おんな has one. Same in おとこのこ and おんなのこ.

Answers for every exercise in the Kanji Workbook N5, Lessons 1 to 3 (kanji 1 to 30, workbook pages 9 to 21). That is 120 items: 10 each in れんしゅう I, れんしゅう II, テスト I and テスト II, for each of the three lessons. The workbook's own answer key is at the back of the full book and was not in the pages you shared, so these answers were worked out from the lessons and the word lists. Use this file together with the Kanji 1 Reviewer.

How the exercises work

  • れんしゅう I: write the hiragana reading of the underlined kanji.
  • れんしゅう II: the word is given in hiragana. Write it in kanji and give the English meaning. The workbook's example is おおきい, 大きい, big.
  • テスト I: pick the right hiragana reading from four choices.
  • テスト II: pick the right kanji from four choices.

In the tests, the answer is the number of the correct choice, with the choice itself in brackets.

docs.title: Intensive Japanese 1 Chapter 9 Reviewer
docs.intro: Chapter 9 teaches you to say where you go, where you come from, how you get there, who goes with you and when. You also pick up two small sentence endings, ね and よ, and the big new idea of the chapter: every verb has a second, shorter form called the dictionary form. Everything here comes from pages 131 to 145 of the workbook.
docs.html:
Chapter 9 teaches you to say where you go, where you come from, how you get there, who goes with you and when. You also pick up two small sentence endings, ね and よ, and the big new idea of the chapter: every verb has a second, shorter form called the dictionary form. Everything here comes from pages 131 to 145 of the workbook.

How to use this reviewer

  • Read the grammar once, then cover the English column and try to say each sentence out loud.
  • Learn the vocabulary in the order it appears: nature and places, trip words, the motion verbs, then the countries.
  • Spend the most time on the dictionary form section. It is brand new and it is where most mistakes happen.
  • Skim the mix-ups before the self-test, then do the self-test without peeking at the key.

Grammar: the patterns Chapter 9 teaches, with examples

A motion verb moves you from one place to another: go, come, go home, go back. The verb always comes last, and the small marker after each word tells you its job. All four motion verbs here are in the formal ます forms you know from Chapter 7.

The markers at a glance

MarkerJobQuestion wordExample
へ / にwhere you are heading (to)どこへ / どこに (where)日本へ いきます。
からwhere you come from (from)どこから (where from)フランスから きました。
でthe vehicle you travel in (by)なにで / どうやって (how)バスで かえります。
にone exact time (at, on)なんじに / なんようびに九時に かえります。
から / までstart and end of a time (from, until)なんじから / なんじまで三時から 五時まで
ごろaround a point in timeなんじごろ (around what time)十一時ごろ かえりました。
と / といっしょにwho goes with you (with)だれと / どなたと (with whom)ともだちと いきます。
でhow many of you (number of people)なんにんで (how many)三人で いきます。
ねasking the other person to agree (isn't it?)noneあつかったですね。
よstressing something (emphasis)noneはやいですよ。

どこから and the time questions are not on the workbook's question word list, but they are natural partners of the same markers, so they are here for your practice.

9.1 A は Destination へ・に Motion Verb, and Origin から きました

Say where someone goes with へ or に. The book says the two are interchangeable: へ stresses the direction, and に stresses the point you arrive at. When へ is a marker, it is read e, not he. To say where you came from, use the set phrase から きました.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
わたしは 日本へ いきます。watashi wa nihon e ikimasu.I will go to Japan.
ともだちは いえに きました。tomodachi wa ie ni kimashita.My friend came to my house.
わたしは えいがかんへ いきます。watashi wa eigakan e ikimasu.I will go to the movie theater.
ぶちょうは 日本へ かえります。buchou wa nihon e kaerimasu.The manager will go home to Japan.
アナさんは えきに もどります。Ana-san wa eki ni modorimasu.Ana will return to the train station.
フランスから きました。furansu kara kimashita.I came from France.
キムさんは かんこくから きました。Kimu-san wa kankoku kara kimashita.Kim came from Korea.
スーパーと ぎんこうへ いきました。su-pa- to ginkou e ikimashita.I went to the supermarket and the bank.
  • いきます is go and きます is come. かえります is go home, and もどります is go back to a place you were at before, such as a station or an office.
  • The last example shows と meaning and between two places. It is not the と that means with.
  • Past and negative follow the four endings you already know: いきます, いきません, いきました, いきませんでした.
VerbPresent positivePresent negativePast positivePast negative
goいきますいきませんいきましたいきませんでした
comeきますきませんきましたきませんでした
go homeかえりますかえりませんかえりましたかえりませんでした
go backもどりますもどりませんもどりましたもどりませんでした

9.2 Mode of Transportation で Motion Verb

Put で after the vehicle to say how you travel. The one exception is あるいて (on foot). It already means by walking, so it takes no で.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
毎日 あるいて かえります。mainichi aruite kaerimasu.I walk home every day.
じてんしゃで スーパーへ いきます。jitensha de su-pa- e ikimasu.I go to the supermarket by bicycle.
ははは タクシーで きました。haha wa takushi- de kimashita.My mother came by taxi.
きょねん ふねで いきました。kyonen fune de ikimashita.I went by ship last year.
ひこうきで シンガポールへ いきます。hikouki de shingapo-ru e ikimasu.I will go to Singapore by plane.
バスで いなかへ かえります。basu de inaka e kaerimasu.I will go home to the countryside by bus.
きのう でんしゃで かえりました。kinou densha de kaerimashita.I went home by train yesterday.
ぶちょうは くるまで きました。buchou wa kuruma de kimashita.The manager came by car.

9.3 Time Expression に・から・まで・ごろ Verb

The time words work the way they did in Chapters 7 and 8. Use に for one exact time, such as a clock time, a day of the week or a date. Leave に out with words that are not exact, such as 毎年, きのう, ゆうべ and おとといの よる. With ごろ (around), the book leaves に out too.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
ゆうべ 十一時ごろ かえりました。yuube juuichi-ji goro kaerimashita.I went home around 11 o'clock last night.
きのう くすりやに(は) いきませんでした。kinou kusuriya ni (wa) ikimasen deshita.I did not go to the drugstore yesterday.
おとといの よる 日本から もどりました。ototoi no yoru nihon kara modorimashita.I came back from Japan the night before last.
月よう日に がっこうへ いきません。getsuyoubi ni gakkou e ikimasen.I do not go to school on Monday.
らいしゅうの 土よう日に かえりません。raishuu no doyoubi ni kaerimasen.I will not go home next Saturday.
十二月 二十五日に アメリカへ いきます。juunigatsu nijuugonichi ni amerika e ikimasu.I will go to America on December 25.
たなかさんは 毎年 フィリピンへ いきます。Tanaka-san wa maitoshi firipin e ikimasu.Mr. Tanaka goes to the Philippines every year.
三時はんごろ きました。sanji han goro kimashita.I came around 3:30.
  • The は in くすりやには is the same spotlight trick as を to は in Chapter 8. It puts the focus on that one place: not to the drugstore, at least.
  • Time words that point to the past, like きのう, ゆうべ and おととい, go with ました or ませんでした.

9.4 Companion と・といっしょに Verb

Person + と (or と いっしょに) + verb: the person who goes with you. いっしょに just stresses the word together.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
あさって ともだちと いっしょに いきます。asatte tomodachi to issho ni ikimasu.I will go with my friend the day after tomorrow.
きょねん かぞくと いきました。kyonen kazoku to ikimashita.I went with my family last year.
ははと いっしょに かえりました。haha to issho ni kaerimashita.I went home with my mother.
やまださんと もどりました。Yamada-san to modorimashita.I came back with Mr. Yamada.
キムさんと きました。Kimu-san to kimashita.I came with Kim.
あねと かえります。ane to kaerimasu.I will go home with my older sister.
ぶちょうと もどります。buchou to modorimasu.I will go back with the department head.
アナさんと きます。Ana-san to kimasu.I will come with Ana.

For your own family use the plain words (はは, あね). For someone else's family use the polite ones (おかあさん, おねえさん).

9.5 Counter for people で Verb

Number of people + で + verb: how many of you do it together. The count includes you, so 二人で means two people in total. 一人で means alone.

KanaRomajiEnglish
ひとりhitori1 person
ふたりfutari2 people
さんにんsannin3 people
よにんyonin4 people
ごにんgonin5 people
ろくにんrokunin6 people
しちにん / ななにんshichinin / nananin7 people
はちにんhachinin8 people
きゅうにんkyuunin9 people
じゅうにんjuunin10 people
なんにんnanninhow many people

One and two people are special words. From three on it is the number plus にん, and four is よにん, not しにん.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
二人で こうえんに いきました。futari de kouen ni ikimashita.The two of us went to the park.
きのう 一人で かえりました。kinou hitori de kaerimashita.I went home alone yesterday.
三人で レストランで たべます。sannin de resutoran de tabemasu.The three of us eat at a restaurant.
一人で あそびました。hitori de asobimashita.I played alone.
十人で いきます。juunin de ikimasu.Ten of us will go.
クラスメートと 二人で いきました。kurasume-to to futari de ikimashita.I went with a classmate, just the two of us.
四人で かえります。yonin de kaerimasu.The four of us will go home.
六人で もどります。rokunin de modorimasu.The six of us will go back.

Asking with question words

The question word takes the same marker its answer will take. Swap the question word for the real answer and the marker stays put.

MarkerQuestion wordsAsks forMeaning
へ / にどこへ / どこにdestinationwhere?
でなにで / どうやってmode of transportationhow?
とだれと / どなたとcompanionwith whom?
でなんにんでnumber of peoplehow many?
QuestionAnswerEnglish
毎日 なにで かいしゃへ いきますか。ちかてつで かいしゃへ いきます。How do you go to the company every day? I go by subway.
なんにんで パーティーに いきましたか。さんにんで パーティーに いきました。How many of you went to the party? Three of us.
毎晚 どうやって かえりますか。バスで かえります。How do you go home every night? By bus.
なにで びょういんに いきましたか。タクシーで いきました。How did you go to the hospital? By taxi.
おととい だれと もどりましたか。すずきさんと もどりました。Who did you come back with the day before yesterday? With Mr. Suzuki.

9.6 〜ね (isn't it?)

Put ね at the end of a sentence when you expect the other person to agree. Think of it as isn't it, right or don't you think. The reply そうですね means yes, I agree.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
A: きのう あつかったですね。A: kinou atsukatta desu ne.It was hot yesterday, wasn't it?
B: そうですね。B: sou desu ne.Yes, it was hot (I agree with you).
A: かいぎは はじまりましたね。A: kaigi wa hajimarimashita ne.The meeting has started, right?
B: はい、そうですね。B: hai, sou desu ne.Yes, it has.
A: それは たいへんですね。A: sore wa taihen desu ne.That is difficult, isn't it?
B: ええ、そうですね。B: ee, sou desu ne.Yes, it is.
A: ちょっと とおいですね。A: chotto tooi desu ne.It is a little far, isn't it?
B: そうですね。B: sou desu ne.Yes, I think so too.

9.7 〜よ (emphasis)

Put よ at the end of a sentence to push the point: this is the answer, and I am telling you. It is good for correcting someone or giving news the other person may not know.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish
A: せんせいは 日本人ですね。A: sensei wa nihonjin desu ne.The teacher is Japanese, right?
B: いいえ、インド人ですよ。B: iie, indojin desu yo.No, he or she is Indian!
A: タクシーは はやいですか。A: takushi- wa hayai desu ka.Is the taxi fast?
B: はやいですよ。B: hayai desu yo.Yes, it is fast!
A: フランスの ワインは おいしいですか。A: furansu no wain wa oishii desu ka.Is French wine good?
B: おいしいですよ。B: oishii desu yo.Yes, it is good!
ADZの ビルは あれですよ。ADZ no biru wa are desu yo.That is the ADZ Building!
かいしゃの レポートを かきましたよ。kaisha no repo-to o kakimashita yo.I wrote the company report!

Quick test: ね asks the other person to agree. よ tells the other person something. Use ね when you are sure they will nod, and よ when you are adding or fixing information.

MASU-form and dictionary form: two forms of every verb

Every verb has a formal form that ends in ます, and a dictionary form. The dictionary form is the one you look up in a dictionary, and it sounds casual, so the book also calls it the informal form. Cut ます off a verb and what is left is the stem (the book calls it the pre-MASU form or stem form). For example, のみます becomes のみ.

The book sorts verbs into three types, and the names are the book's own:

Book's nameWhat it meansClue in the ます formExamples
Irregular verbsthe stem ends in an い sound, and the last sound shifts to change form-imasuのみます, かきます, あそびます
Regular verbsthe stem ends in え (or sometimes い), and you only add or drop る-emasuたべます, みます
Special verbsfixed forms that you simply memorizeします, きますする, くる

Other books call the book's irregular verbs u-verbs (godan) and its regular verbs ru-verbs (ichidan). The names differ, but the verbs are the same.

From ます form to dictionary form

TypeStep 1Step 2Examples
Irregular (-imasu)remove ますchange the last sound from the い row to the う rowのみます → のみ → のむ, かきます → かき → かく
Regular (-emasu)remove ますadd るたべます → たべ → たべる, みます → み → みる
Specialnone, the form is fixedします → する, きます → くる

The last sound shifts like this:

ends in (ます side)みきぎしちいにびり
becomes (dictionary side)むくぐすつうぬぶる
exampleのみます → のむかきます → かくおよぎます → およぐはなします → はなすまちます → まつかいます → かうしにます → しぬあそびます → あそぶわかります → わかる

Watch out when you go in this direction. A few regular verbs also end in -imasu, such as みます (みる) and おきます (おきる). From the ます form alone you cannot always tell, so learn those as pairs.

From dictionary form to ます form

TypeClue in the dictionary formStep 1Step 2Examples
Irregularends in ぶ, む, ぬ, ぐ, す, く, う, つ, or る after あ, う or おchange the last sound from the う row to the い rowadd ますのむ → のみ → のみます, かく → かき → かきます
Regularends in える or いるremove るadd ますたべる → たべ → たべます, みる → み → みます
Specialする, くるfixedする → します, くる → きます

The book's step box leaves out う and つ, but its table on the next page includes them, so use the table below.

The book's verb table, with the ending groups

Book's groupDictionary form ends inDictionary formます formMeaning
1ぶあそぶあそびますenjoy, play
1むのむのみますdrink
1ぬしぬしにますdie
2ぐおよぐおよぎますswim
3すはなすはなしますspeak
4くかくかきますwrite
5うかうかいますbuy
5つまつまちますwait
5る after あわかるわかりますunderstand
5る after ううるうりますsell
5る after おのるのりますride
5 (starred)くいくいきますgo
5 (starred)るかえるかえりますgo home
Regularえるたべるたべますeat
Regularいるみるみますwatch
Specialするするしますdo
Specialくるくるきますcome

The book puts a star on いく and かえる. かえる is the real trap: it ends in える like a regular verb, but it acts like an irregular one, so it is かえります and not かえます. The book names はいる (enter), はしる (run), きる (cut) and しる (know) as the same kind of trap. いく is starred too, but its ます form follows the normal く rule: いく becomes いきます.

A quick way to tell the type

  1. Is it する or くる, or a noun plus する such as かいものする? It is a special verb.
  2. Does it end in える or いる? It is a regular verb, unless it is one of the traps (かえる, はいる, はしる, きる, しる).
  3. Anything else is an irregular verb. Shift the last sound.

Useful lines from the Review readings

The letter from Jon to Ana and the summer trip passage are full of lines you can borrow.

JapaneseRomajiEnglish

Which verb goes with which place

There is an important split here. Going verbs use へ or に for the place you head to. Activity verbs (あそびます, およぎます, かいものします) use で for the place where you do the activity.

Easy to mix up

These are the spots where Chapter 9 trips most people up. Each row gives you a quick test you can run in your head.

Markers that look alike

Mix-upQuick testExample
へ / に (heading to) vs に (exact time)After a place, へ or に means to. After a time word, に means at or on.うみへ いきます (I go to the sea) vs 九時に いきます (I go at nine)
へ vs で with a placeGoing to a place takes へ or に. Doing something at a place takes で.うみへ いきます (I go to the sea) vs うみで およぎます (I swim in the sea)
で (vehicle) vs で (number of people)Look at the word before it. A vehicle says how you travel. A number of people says how many of you.バスで (by bus) vs 三人で (three of us)
と (with) vs と (and)と right before the verb means with. と between two places or nouns means and.ともだちと いきます (I go with a friend) vs スーパーと ぎんこうへ いきます (I go to the supermarket and the bank)
から (from a place) vs から (from a time)Place + から + きました means came from. Time + から + まで means from and until.フランスから きました vs 九時から 五時まで
に with time wordsUse に with an exact time. Leave it out with 毎年, きのう, ゆうべ and おととい, and after ごろ.月よう日に いきます vs 毎年 いきます, 三時ごろ きます
あるいてあるいて already means on foot, so it never takes で.あるいて かえります vs バスで かえります
へ as a markerWhen へ is a marker, it is read e, not he.日本へ いきます is nihon e ikimasu

Verbs that look or sound alike

GroupHow to keep them straight
いきます / きますいきます is go and きます is come. They take the same markers. Only the direction changes.
いきます / いますOne sound apart. いきます is go, and います is to be somewhere (people and animals).
かえります / もどりますかえります is go home, to where you live or belong. もどります is go back to a place you were at before, such as a station or an office.
かえります / かいます / かけますOne sound apart. かえり is go home, かい is buy, かけ is call (a phone).
きます / ききます / きりますきます is come, ききます is listen or ask, きります is cut.
あそびます / およぎますBoth are activity verbs. あそび is play, およぎ is swim. Both take で for the place.

Dictionary form traps

TrapWhat to rememberExample
Ends in える or いる but is not regularかえる, はいる, はしる, きる and しる follow the irregular rule even though they look regular.かえる → かえります, not かえます
Ends in -imasu but is regularみます and おきます end in -imasu, but they are regular verbs. Just add る.みます → みる, おきます → おきる
いくThe book puts a star on it. The ます form is the normal いきます.いく → いきます
Verbs ending in うう changes to い before ます.すう → すいます, かう → かいます
Verbs ending in つつ changes to ち before ます.まつ → まちます
Verbs ending in ぬぬ changes to に before ます.しぬ → しにます
くる vs きるくる is come and is a special verb. きる is cut and is an irregular verb.くる → きます vs きる → きります

WordMeaningsExample
かえりますgo home, return日本へ かえります (I go home to Japan)
はやいfast, earlyタクシーは はやいですよ (The taxi is fast!)
かかりますtakes (time)五じかん かかります (It takes five hours)

Little words that travel together

PairRuleExample
ごろ vs ぐらいごろ is around a point in time. ぐらい is about an amount of time or money.十一時ごろ (around 11:00) vs 五じかんぐらい (about five hours)
Past time wordsきのう, ゆうべ, おととい and せんしゅう point to the past, so the verb ends in ました or ませんでした.きのう くすりやには いきませんでした
一人で / 二人でThe count includes you. 一人で is alone, and 二人で is two people in all.クラスメートと 二人で いきました
ね vs よね asks the other person to nod. よ tells the other person something.あつかったですね vs インド人ですよ
そうですねThe usual reply to ね. It means yes, I agree.A: たいへんですね。 B: そうですね。
なにで / どうやってBoth ask how you travel, and both are answered with a vehicle plus で.どうやって かえりますか。 バスで かえります。
毎年, 毎日, 毎朝, 毎晚Habit words take no に.毎年 フィリピンへ いきます

Verb conjugation (page 132)

The first row (いきます) is given. Fill in the other three. The four endings never change: -masu, -masen, -mashita, -masen deshita.

Change to negative (page 135)

The book's example turns あした スーパーへ いきます into あした スーパーへ いきません. A present sentence takes ません. A past sentence takes ませんでした.

#AnswerNote
1イギリスへ かえりません。Present, so ません.

The book's example also swaps あした for きのう. None of these sentences has a time word to swap, so only the verb changes. A positive verb becomes ました. A negative verb becomes ませんでした.

5きのう 何時ごろ かえりましたか。きのう 五時ごろ かえりました。I went home around five yesterday.
6スーパーへ いきますか。なんようびに いきますか。はい、いきます。日よう日に いきます。Yes, I go. I go on Sundays.

9ときどき モールへ いきますか。だれと いきますか。はい、ときどき いきます。ともだちと いきます。Yes, sometimes. I go with friends.
10がいこくへ いきましたか。どこへ いきましたか。はい、いきました。シンガポールへ いきました。Yes, I went. I went to Singapore.

A negative answer also works. For number 8 or number 10 you could say いいえ、いきませんでした。 (No, I did not go.)

Review VI: Translate into Japanese (page 145)

#EnglishAnswerNotes
1I came from Korea.かんこくから きました。から きました says where you came from.
2Every day I go by subway to the office.毎日 ちかてつで オフィスへ いきます。No に after 毎日. で for the vehicle, へ for the destination.
3I will return to Japan next week.らいしゅう 日本へ かえります。No に after らいしゅう. もどります also works.
4Did you come by bus this morning?けさ バスで きましたか。No に after けさ. Past tense.
5I will go to the embassy this week.こんしゅう たいしかんへ いきます。No に after こんしゅう.
6What time will you go home tonight?こんばん 何時に かえりますか。何時に asks for an exact time. 何時ごろ works if you mean around what time.
7Yesterday, I went home by myself.きのう 一人で かえりました。一人で means alone.
8I will go home by taxi this evening.こんばん タクシーで かえります。こんばん covers both tonight and this evening.

Word order can shift a little in all of these, as long as the verb stays last.

docs.html:
Chapter 10 teaches you how to talk the way friends and family talk. You learn to turn action nouns into verbs with する (べんきょうする, そうじする), to change the polite ます forms into plain forms (たべる, たべない, たべた, たべなかった), and to add the casual endings の and わ. Everything here comes from pages 146 to 161 of the workbook.

How to use this reviewer

  • Read the grammar once. Then cover the plain-form columns and say each one out loud from the polite form.
  • Learn the vocabulary in the order it appears: action nouns, sports and games, then the new verbs. The verb bank at the end of that section shows every verb in all four plain forms.
  • Skim the mix-ups before the self-test, then do the self-test without peeking at the key.

Grammar: the patterns Chapter 10 teaches, with examples

Two big ideas run through this chapter. First, a noun that names an action can become a verb just by adding する. Second, the polite ます forms from Chapter 7 have casual twins, called the plain forms, and those are what friends and family actually say. The last two patterns, の and わ, are sentence endings that give casual speech its flavor.

The chapter at a glance

PatternWhat it doesExample
Noun + する (します)turns an action noun into a verbべんきょうする (to study)
Dictionary formplain present positiveたべる
ない formplain present negativeたべない
た formplain past positiveたべた
なかった formplain past negativeたべなかった
のcasual question endingいくの? (Are you going?)
わsoft ending, used by womenいくわ (I'm going.)

10.1 Noun + する (します)

A noun verb is built by adding する to a noun that names an action. べんきょう (study) + する = べんきょうする, to study. Only the する part changes, so the whole verb follows する in every form: します, しません, しました, しませんでした in polite speech, and しない, した, しなかった in plain speech. Sports work the same way: テニス + する means play tennis. You will also see を in front of する, as in ゲームを する (play a game).

Informal (plain) verb forms

In Chapter 7 you learned the formal ます forms. Friends, family and casual speech use plain forms instead, and each polite ending has a plain partner:

~ませんでした~なかったpast negative

How you build the plain forms depends on the type of verb. The workbook uses three names: Irregular verbs (the u-verbs, split into five groups by their last sound), Regular verbs (the る-verbs) and Special verbs (する and くる).

Here is the pattern behind the table. Find the last sound of the dictionary form and the rest follows:

  • The なかった form is the ない form with い swapped for かった: のまない becomes のまなかった.
  • The workbook marks two verbs with a star as exceptions. いく (go) would be いいた by the く rule, but it is いった. かえる (go home) ends in える, so it looks like a Regular verb, but it behaves like a Group 5 verb. The footnote adds しる (know), はいる (enter), はしる (run) and きる (cut) to the list of look-alikes.

Ending markers: の and わ

The two endings attach differently depending on the word in front of them:

Word before itの (casual question)わ (female speaker's ending)Example
Plain verb+ の+ わいくの? / いくわ
い-adjective+ の+ わおいしいの? / おいしいわ
な-adjective+ なの+ だわきれいなの? / きれいだわ
Noun+ なの+ だわイギリス人なの? / イギリス人だわ

10.2 の: the casual question marker

In casual speech you drop か, switch the verb to its plain form and add の, with your voice rising at the end.

Polite questionCasual questionRomajiEnglish

10.3 わ: a soft ending for a female speaker

The marker わ is commonly used by women to affirm an opinion, to clarify something and to express an emotion. It makes a sentence sound softer. After a noun or a な-adjective it becomes だわ.

Easy to mix up

These are the spots where Chapter 10 trips most people up. Each row gives you a quick test you can run in your head.

Building the plain forms

Mix-upQuick testExample
う verbs use わ, not あBefore ない, a verb ending in う changes う into わ.かう > かわない (not かあない), すう > すわない
く verbs give いた, except いくThe past of a verb ending in く is いた. いく is the one exception and gives いった.かく > かいた, but いく > いった
ぐ gives いだ, く gives いたThe voiced ぐ gets the voiced ending だ.およぐ > およいだ, かく > かいた
A verb ending in る: Regular or Group 5?After あ, う or お the verb is always Group 5. After い or え it is usually Regular.わかる > わからない (Group 5), たべる > たべない (Regular)
The look-alikes the workbook starsかえる, しる and はいる end in える or いる but still act like Group 5 verbs.かえる > かえらない, かえった (not かえない, かえた)
Which past ending? Sort by the last soundむ, ぶ, ぬ give んだ. く gives いた. ぐ gives いだ. す gives した. う, つ, る give った.のむ > のんだ, はなす > はなした, まつ > まった
しぬ has a double なぬ becomes な before ない, so the two な sit side by side.しぬ > しなない, しななかった
くる changes its stem every timeThree different stems: く, こ, き.くる, こない, きた, こなかった
Noun + するOnly the する part changes. The noun stays put.べんきょうしない, べんきょうした, べんきょうしなかった

Verbs and nouns that look or sound alike

GroupHow to keep them straight
そうじ / そうだんOne sound apart. そうじ is cleaning, そうだん is consultation.
せつめい / せんたくBoth start with せ. せつめい is explanation, せんたく is laundry.
しょうかい / しょうせつしょうかい is introduction (Chapter 10). しょうせつ is a novel (Chapter 8).
しる / しぬ / するThree short verbs that start with the same sound. しる is know, しぬ is die, する is do.
つかう / つくるOne sound apart. つかう is use, つくる is make or cook.
まつ / もつOne vowel apart. まつ is wait, もつ is hold or carry.
おぼえる / おしえるおぼえる is to remember. おしえる is to teach or tell.
わかる / しるわかる is understand. しる is know, as in come to know a fact or a person.
はなみ / はなびThe last sound tells you. み is look, so はなみ is flower viewing. び is fire, so はなび is fireworks.
あるく / あるあるく is walk. ある (あります) is to exist, for things.

Endings and markers that look alike

Mix-upQuick testExample
の at the end vs の in the middleAt the very end, with a rising voice, の asks a question. In the middle it links two nouns.かいぎ おわったの? vs 日本の おんがく
わ vs はThe sentence ending is わ. The topic marker is は, even though both sound like wa.いくわ vs わたしは いく
なの / だわ vs の / わNouns and な-adjectives need なの and だわ. Verbs and い-adjectives take の and わ directly.きれいなの? / きれいだわ vs いくの? / いくわ
だよ vs よだ shows up in front of よ only after a noun or a な-adjective.だいじょうぶだよ vs いくよ
よ vs ねよ tells someone something. ね looks for agreement.いくよ (I'm going, you know) vs とおいね (It's far, isn't it?)
Markers that can disappearThe workbook says を, が, に and へ are sometimes dropped in casual speech. Keep the other markers.しんぶん(を) よむ
を into は in a negativeを can turn into は. は can also follow に or へ for more emphasis.きょうの 5じには おわらない

Little words that travel together

PairRuleExample
ぜんぜん or あまり + negativeBoth need a ない ending. ぜんぜん means not at all, あまり means not very much.あまり たべない (I hardly eat it)
Time word decides the tenseA present time word takes the present form. A past time word takes the past form.まいにち よむ vs きのう よんだ
A past time word plus ぜんぜんUse the past negative.おとといは ぜんぜん べんきょうしなかった
A length of timeIt takes no marker.六時間 うんてんした (I drove for six hours)
ひとり vs ひとりでひとり is one person. ひとりで means alone.ひとりで はなびを みる
Counting peopleOnly one, two and four are special.ひとり, ふたり, さんにん, よにん (not よんにん), ごにん
ごろ vs ぐらいごろ is around a point in time. ぐらい is about an amount.九時ごろ (around nine) vs 二時間ぐらい (about two hours)

Three to watch. Number 11 いく gives いった, not いいた. Numbers 16 and 17 end in える and いる but are Group 5, so they are かえらない and しらない, not かえない and しない. And number 10 すう uses わ before ない: すわない.

Change the verbs to past tense (page 154)

The example is おちゃを のむ > おちゃを のんだ.

#SentenceAnswerWhy
1けいたいを うる。けいたいを うった。Group 5: る becomes った.
2えいがを みる。えいがを みた。Regular: drop る, add た.
3あさごはんを たべない。あさごはんを たべなかった。A negative stays negative: ない becomes なかった.
4きょうかしょを よむ。きょうかしょを よんだ。Group 1: む becomes んだ.
5あいみさんは およがない。あいみさんは およがなかった。ない becomes なかった.
6水よう日に やすむ。水よう日に やすんだ。Group 1: む becomes んだ.
7くつを かわない。くつを かわなかった。ない becomes なかった.
8大学で えいごを おしえる。大学で えいごを おしえた。Regular: drop る, add た.
9金よう日に くる。金よう日に きた。Special: くる becomes きた.
10ともだちと あそぶ。ともだちと あそんだ。Group 1: ぶ becomes んだ.

Change the verbs to negative (page 154)

The example is レストランで たべる > レストランで たべない.

#SentenceAnswerWhy
1一人で いく。一人で いかない。く becomes か, then ない.
2らいしゅうの 火よう日に やすむ。らいしゅうの 火よう日に やすまない。む becomes ま, then ない.
3みんなに せつめいした。みんなに せつめいしなかった。The sentence is past, so the negative is the past negative しなかった.
4はしで たべる。はしで たべない。Regular: drop る, add ない.
5日本で はたらいた。日本で はたらかなかった。Past, so the past negative. The verb is はたらく: く becomes か, then なかった.
6来年 もどる。来年 もどらない。Group 5: る becomes ら, then ない.
7きっぷを かった。きっぷを かわなかった。Past of かう. う becomes わ, then なかった.
8メールを かく。メールを かかない。く becomes か, then ない.
9でんしゃで いった。でんしゃで いかなかった。Past of いく, so the past negative いかなかった.
10土よう日に せんたくする。土よう日に せんたくしない。Only する changes: しない.

Review I: Choose the correct grammatical pattern (page 157)

#AnswerWhy
11 つくる毎日 shows a habit, so use the present positive. つかう (use) does not fit りょうり.
22 たべないあまり needs a negative, and 毎朝 is present.
34 のんだせんしゅう is last week, so use the past. のんだ is the real past of のむ. The other choices are not words.
42 かわないThe computer is expensive, so right now you will not buy it. う becomes わ before ない. かあない is not a word.
51 おきたけさ is in the past. おきる is Regular, so drop る and add た.
63 だわきれい is a な-adjective, so a woman's ending is だわ. B is saying yes, it is very pretty.
74 うんてんくるまを うんてんする means drive a car.
84 まったB answers in the past (まちました), so A asks in the past. まつ is Group 5: つ becomes った.

Review II: Rearrange the words (page 158)

The Order column lists the option numbers from left to right across the four blanks.

#OrderFull sentenceMeaning
14 1 3 2わたしは まいにち ゲームを する。I play games every day.
24 3 1 2明日の パーティーへ こないの。Aren't you coming to tomorrow's party?
34 2 1 3やまださんは まいしゅう きんようびに へやを そうじする。Mr. Yamada cleans his room every week on Friday.
42 1 4 3きのうの よる タイ人の ともだちと はなびを みた。Last night I watched fireworks with a Thai friend.
53 2 4 1いもうとは まいあさ ぜんぜん はやく おきない。My younger sister does not get up early at all in the morning.
64 1 3 2おとうさんは おさけとコーラを あまり のまない。My father doesn't drink alcohol or cola very much.
73 1 4 2わたしは きのう こうえんの まえで まった。Yesterday I waited in front of the park.
82 4 1 3きょねん キムさんと 日本語を 日本で べんきょうした。Last year I studied Japanese in Japan with Kim.

Notes on a few. Number 2 ends with の as a casual question: こないの (aren't you coming?). Number 4 pairs タイ人の with ともだち, since 人 is a person, and the fireworks come last before を. Number 5 puts ぜんぜん right before はやく because it cancels the idea of getting up early, and another order of the middle words may also be accepted. Number 8 starts with と because キムさん comes just before the blanks.

Review III: Fill in the proper word or phrase (page 159)

The passage is about a family trip to Sapporo last February.

#AnswerFull phraseWhy
(1)4 きせつふゆの きせつは とても さむかったですThe winter season was very cold. The other choices (photo, game, laundry) do not fit.
(2)4 ごにんちちと ははと あねと あにと ごにんで いきましたFather, mother, older sister and older brother, plus the writer, makes five people.
(3)1 たのしかったとても たのしかったですThe trip was last year, so use the past of the い-adjective たのしい.

Review IV: Read and answer (page 160)

The passage is a letter from Ana to John. She watched the cherry blossoms with friends from the company last Sunday, she sometimes works until eight, and she goes back to the Philippines on the 15th of next month.

#AnswerWhy
11 こうえんShe saw the cherry blossoms (はなみ) with friends from the company at a park: こうえんで 花見を 見ました.
24 ひとりで かえりますThe letter says only that she goes home to the Philippines on the 15th. It names no one to go with, so alone is the best fit. If your class discussed a different reading, go with your teacher.

Review V: Questions and answers in sentence form (page 161)

These ask about you, so the answers below are samples. The questions are casual, so the samples are casual too. With a teacher, use the polite ます forms instead. Any true answer in a full sentence works. In number 1, the dot between the two questions means or, so answer with either one.

#QuestionSample answerMeaning
1何時から 何時まで べんきょうするの・しごとするの?九時から 五時まで しごとする。I work from nine to five.
2毎日 にほんご べんきょうするの? いっしゅうかんに なんじかん べんきょうするの?はい、毎日 べんきょうする。いっしゅうかんに 十時間ぐらい べんきょうする。Yes, I study every day. About ten hours a week.
3いちにちに どのぐらい けいたいを つかうの?いちにちに 三時間ぐらい つかう。I use it about three hours a day.
4日本のりょうりを たべる? どこで たべる?はい、たべる。レストランで たべる。Yes, I eat it. I eat it at a restaurant.
5スポーツするの? なんの スポーツする?はい、する。テニスする。Yes, I do. I play tennis.
6先月 えいがを みたの? なにを みたの?はい、みた。日本の えいがを みた。Yes, I watched one. I watched a Japanese movie.
7まいしゅう へや そうじするの?はい、まいしゅう 日よう日に そうじする。Yes, I clean it every week on Sunday.
8ことしの クリスマスやすみは どこ いくの?かぞくと セブへ いく。I'm going to Cebu with my family.
9今月 モールに いったの? モールで なにを したの?はい、いった。かいものした。Yes, I went. I went shopping.
10土よう日に どこへ いくの?土よう日に ともだちの いえへ いく。I'm going to my friend's house on Saturday.

A negative answer also works. For example, for number 5 you could say いいえ、しない。 (No, I don't.)

Review VI: Translate into Japanese (page 161)

The answers are in casual style because this chapter is about plain forms. Each note gives the polite version too.

#EnglishAnswerNotes
1I will go out with my friends tonight.こんばん ともだちと いく。Polite: こんばん ともだちと いきます。 と is for the companion. でかける (go out) also works when no place is named.
2I will consult my teacher tomorrow.あした せんせいに そうだんする。Polite: あした せんせいに そうだんします。 に is for the person you consult.
3I will explain to my classmates.クラスメートに せつめいする。Polite: クラスメートに せつめいします。 クラスメート (kurasume-to) is new here, and ともだちに also works. に is for the listeners.
4I practice at the school every day.まいにち がっこうで れんしゅうする。Polite: まいにち がっこうで れんしゅうします。 で is for the place. まいにち takes no に.
5I drove the car for 6 hours yesterday.きのう 六時間 くるまを うんてんした。Polite: きのう 六時間 くるまを うんてんしました。 A length of time takes no marker.
6I will play golf with my friend this Sunday.こんしゅうの 日よう日に ともだちと ゴルフする。Polite: こんしゅうの 日よう日に ともだちと ゴルフします。 A sport plus する means play it.
7I clean the room once a week.いっしゅうかんに いっかい へやを そうじする。Polite: いっしゅうかんに いっかい へやを そうじします。 に after いっしゅうかん means per.
8I submit reports to my supervisor every Monday.まいしゅう 月よう日に かちょうに レポートを だす。Polite: まいしゅう 月よう日に かちょうに レポートを だします。 かちょう (section chief) stands in for supervisor. に is for the person who receives the report.
9I do not play tennis.テニスしない。Polite: テニスしません。 Only する changes. テニスは しない also works to stress tennis.
10I will watch the fireworks alone tonight.こんばん ひとりで はなびを みる。Polite: こんばん ひとりで はなびを みます。 ひとりで means alone.

Word order can shift a little in all of these, as long as the verb stays last.

docs.intro: The Kanji Workbook N5 teaches kanji 31 to 60 in three more lessons: time words (half, minute, hour, week, year), then the parts of the day and the four seasons, then directions and positions. This reviewer covers all 30 kanji with strokes, meanings and readings, every word the workbook uses, the look-alikes and reading traps, and a self-test. The answers to the workbook's own exercises are in the separate answer key. Kanji 1 to 30 are in the Kanji 1 Reviewer.
docs.html:
The Kanji Workbook N5 teaches kanji 31 to 60 in three more lessons: time words (half, minute, hour, week, year), then the parts of the day and the four seasons, then directions and positions. This reviewer covers all 30 kanji with strokes, meanings and readings, every word the workbook uses, the look-alikes and reading traps, and a self-test. The answers to the workbook's own exercises are in the separate answer key. Kanji 1 to 30 are in the Kanji 1 Reviewer.

How to use this reviewer

  • Cover the readings, look at the kanji, and say the reading and the meaning.
  • Write each kanji by hand a few times and check your stroke count against the table.
  • Learn the words in the vocabulary tables, because most readings only make sense inside a word.
  • Say the time and counting cheat sheets out loud. The sound changes are where most mistakes happen.
  • Finish with the mix-ups and the self-test.

Kanji list

Reading notes for Kanji 2

The same two kinds of reading from Kanji 1 apply here. The Japanese reading (kun'yomi) is meaning-based and usually appears when a kanji stands alone or has kana after it. The Chinese reading (on'yomi) is sound-based and usually appears inside compound words.

  • The workbook marks special readings with a star. In this set they are 時けい (とけい), 今年 (ことし), 今日 (きょう), 今朝 (けさ) and 下手な (へたな). The tables below write "special" instead of the star.
  • A reading in square brackets is listed for completeness, but the workbook gives no example words for it, such as [なかば], [ちょう], [か], [しゅん], [とう], [しゅう], [ほく], [なん] and [せい].
  • "None" means the workbook shows no reading of that kind for the kanji.
  • The Chinese reading column also shows the sound changes you meet inside words, such as ぷん and ぶん for 分.
  • The Strokes column shows the number the workbook gives.
  • Many example words reuse kanji from Kanji 1, like 一, 日, 月 and 人, so keep that reviewer close.

Lesson 4: kanji 31 to 40

These ten kanji are the language of time: half, minutes, hours, weeks and years, plus the words for this, last, next and every. 時, 週 and 年 all join with 間 to say how long something lasts.

#KanjiStrokesMeaningJapanese readingChinese reading
31半5half[なかば]はん
32分4division, minutesわ(かる)ふん (ぷん, ぶん)
33時10timeとき, とけい (special)じ
34週11weeknoneしゅう
35年6year, ageことし (special), とし (in まいとし)ねん
36間12intervalあいだかん
37今4nowいま, きょう (special), けさ (special)こん
38先6ahead, last ~さき(に)せん
39来7come, next ~く(る), き(ます)らい
40毎6every ~noneまい

今 has the most readings in this lesson: いま on its own, こん in 今週, 今月 and 今晩, and the two special ones, きょう and けさ.

Lesson 5: kanji 41 to 50

These are the parts of the day, the four seasons, and 正 (correct), which you will meet again in New Year (正月). The workbook lists the seasons in the usual order: spring, summer, autumn, winter.

午 on its own means noon, and it never appears alone. You will only see it in 午前 (a.m.) and 午後 (p.m.). 今朝 is listed under both 今 and 朝, with the special reading けさ.

Lesson 6: kanji 51 to 60

These are positions and directions: up, down, left, right, inside, outside and the four points of the compass. Most are read with the Japanese reading, because they are everyday place words.

#KanjiStrokesMeaningJapanese readingChinese reading

左 and 右 take their Chinese readings only together, in 左右 (さゆう, left and right). 下手な (へたな) is the special partner of 上手 (じょうず), and the 手 in both is a kanji you have not learned yet. In the workbook's compass picture, 北 is at the top, 南 at the bottom, 西 on the left and 東 on the right.

Cheat sheets

These are the patterns that show up again and again in this set. Say each table out loud once, then cover the Kana column and test yourself.

Cheat sheet: clock times

Add 時 (じ) to the number. Three hours are traps: 4 o'clock is よじ (not よんじ), 7 o'clock is しちじ (not ななじ) and 9 o'clock is くじ (not きゅうじ).

The workbook's examples use 一時, 三時, 四時, 六時, 七時, 八時, 九時, 十時 and 何時. The rest follow the same pattern.

Cheat sheet: minutes

Add 分 to the number. The sound is ふん after 2, 5, 7 and 9, and ぷん after 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 何. A small っ appears before ぷん after 1, 6, 8 and 10.

Every count that ends in 十, such as 二十分 (にじゅっぷん) and 三十分 (さんじゅっぷん), ends in じゅっぷん. 半分 is the one to watch: it is はんぶん with a ぶ, not はんふん. The workbook shows 一分, 二分, 六分, 十分, 三十分 and 半分. A few of these also have a second reading in everyday speech (七分 as しちふん, 八分 as はちふん, 十分 as じっぷん), but the forms in the table are the ones to learn first.

Cheat sheet: clock time or length of time

Without 間, 時 is a point on the clock. With 間 (かん) it counts hours. 半 (はん) always goes last.

Cheat sheet: how long (hours, weeks, years)

Add 間 to a count to say how long something lasts. 週間 counts weeks and 年間 counts years. Two readings need care: 一週間 has a small っ (いっしゅうかん), and 四年間 is よねんかん, not よんねんかん or しねんかん.

Months use か月 (かげつ), which you learned in Kanji 1, as in 三か月 (さんかげつ). Days use 日間, as in 五日間 (いつかかん, 5 days), which appears in the workbook's exercises.

Cheat sheet: last, this, next and every

Look at the middle kanji of each word and you can read the time. 先 means last, 今 means this, 来 means next and 毎 means every.

Three oddities: 今年 is ことし (special), 毎月 is まいつき (not まいげつ) and 毎年 is まいとし (not まいねん). Also, 今月 is こんげつ and not こんつき.

Easy to mix up

Most kanji mistakes come from two places: kanji that look alike, and readings that change from word to word. Skim all three tables before any quiz.

Look-alike kanji

Look-alikesHow to tell them apart
千 午 年千 (thousand, from Kanji 1) is a slanted hat over a single bar. 午 (noon) has two bars under its hat. 年 (year) has six strokes and is busier than both. 千 was a wrong choice for 午 in the workbook.
先 生先 (ahead, last) stands on two legs 儿. 生 (as in 先生, teacher) rests on a long flat bar. 生 was a wrong choice for 先 in the workbook.
前 後前 (front) opens with two dots like a hat and ends with 月 and a small knife 刂. 後 (back) has the step radical 彳 on its left side.
間 門 聞 問間 (interval) is 日 inside the gate 門. 聞 puts an ear 耳 in the gate, and 問 puts a mouth 口 in it. The workbook used 門, 聞 and 問 as wrong choices for 間.
夏 百夏 (summer) has a flat bar and a box on top, a bit like 百 (hundred), and it stands on legs 夂. The workbook used 百, 頭 and 頃 as wrong choices. 頭 (head) and 頃 (about) are not taught in this workbook.
春 夏 秋 冬春 (spring) stacks 三, 人 and 日, with the sun at the bottom. 夏 (summer) is the one with 夂 legs. 秋 (autumn) is grain 禾 next to fire 火. 冬 (winter) is the smallest: 夂 over two small drops.
朝 晩朝 (morning) has the moon 月 on its right side. 晩 (night) has the sun 日 on its left side.
左 右 石左 (left) has 工 under the bar and starts with the flat stroke. 右 (right) has 口 under the bar and starts with the slanting stroke. You eat with your right hand, and 口 is the mouth. 石 (stone) has the slanting stroke hanging from the left end of the bar, like a cliff over 口. 石 was a wrong choice for 右 in the workbook.
上 下The short mark sits above the long line in 上 (up) and below it in 下 (down).
中中 (inside) is a box 口 with a line straight through the middle.
外 夕 多外 (outside) is 夕 and ト side by side. 夕 and ト were wrong choices in the workbook because they are its two halves. 多 is 夕 twice.
北 南北 (north) looks like two people back to back. 南 (south) starts with a cross 十 on top of a frame.
東 木 来 米東 (east) is the sun 日 inside a tree 木. 木 (tree) is plain. 来 (come) looks like 米 (rice) with the top dot stretched into a flat bar.
西 四 酒西 (west) has a flat lid over a box. 四 (four, from Kanji 1) is a box with two short legs inside. 酒 (sake) has the water mark on its left side.
正 止正 (correct) is 止 (stop) with a flat bar on top.
毎 母毎 (every) is 母 (mother, from Kanji 1) with a small hat on top.

Reading traps

KanjiWatch out forWhat to remember
今いま, こん, きょう, けさいま on its own. こん in 今週, 今月 and 今晩. 今日 is きょう, 今朝 is けさ and 今年 is ことし.
朝あさ or けさあさ in 毎朝 (まいあさ). けさ only in 今朝.
日にち, きょう, かにち in 毎日 (まいにち) and 一日中 (いちにちじゅう). きょう in 今日. か in 五日間 (いつかかん). See the Kanji 1 table for the rest.
月げつ or つきげつ in 今月, 先月 and 来月. つき in 毎月 (まいつき).
年ねん, とし, ことしねん in 来年 and 一年間. とし in 毎年 (まいとし). 今年 is ことし.
時じ, じかん, とき, とけいじ is o'clock (四時 よじ). じかん is how many hours (四時間 よじかん). とき on its own. 時けい is とけい.
四よ, よん, しよ in 四時 (よじ) and 四年間 (よねんかん). よん in 四分 (よんぷん). し in 四月 (しがつ).
分ふん, ぷん, ぶん, わふん after 2, 5, 7 and 9. ぷん after 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 何. ぶん in 半分. わ in 分かる.
半はん半分 is はんぶん. The ぶん belongs to 分, not 半. 一時半 is いちじはん.
週しゅう一週間 is いっしゅうかん with a small っ, but 二週間 is にしゅうかん without one.
間かん or あいだかん after a count (一時間, 二週間, 四年間). あいだ on its own, as in 銀行の間 (between).
先さき or せんさき in 先に. せん in 先生, 先週 and 先月.
来く, き, らいく in 来る. き in 来ます. らい in 来週, 来月 and 来年.
中なか, ちゅう, じゅうなか on its own. ちゅう in 午前中 and 中国. じゅう in 一日中, 一晩中 and 一年中.
前まえ or ぜんまえ on its own and in 名前 (なまえ). ぜん in 午前 (ごぜん).
後あと, うし, ごあと for later. うしろ for back. ご in 午後 and in ~後 (after).
晩ばん今晩 is こんばん, 毎晩 is まいばん and 一晩中 is ひとばんじゅう. Always a voiced ば.
正ただ or しょうただ in 正しい. しょう in 正月 (しょうがつ).
上うえ, うわ, あ, じょううえ on its own, うわ in 上着 (うわぎ), あ in 上げる (あげる), じょう in 上手 (じょうず).
下した, さ, へした on its own, さ in 下げる (さげる), へ in 下手な (へたな).
外そと or がいそと on its own. がい in 外国, 外出 and 海外 (かいがい).
左 右ひだり, みぎ or さゆうひだり and みぎ on their own. Together they are 左右 (さゆう).
東ひがし or とうひがし for the direction. とう in 東京 (とうきょう).
口くち or ぐちThe exit is 北口 (きたぐち), not きたくち. Same for 南口, 東口 and 西口.
春 夏 秋 冬Brackets onlyThe Chinese readings [しゅん], [か], [しゅう] and [とう] have no example words in the workbook. Focus on はる, なつ, あき and ふゆ.

docs.html:
Answers for every exercise in the Kanji Workbook N5, Lessons 4 to 6 (kanji 31 to 60, workbook pages 22 to 36). That is 120 items: 10 each in れんしゅう I, れんしゅう II, テスト I and テスト II, for each of the three lessons. The workbook's own answer key is at the back of the full book and was not in the pages you shared, so these answers were worked out from the lessons and the word lists. Use this file together with the Kanji 2 Reviewer.

How the exercises work

  • れんしゅう I: write the hiragana reading of the underlined kanji.
  • れんしゅう II: the word is given in hiragana. Write it in kanji and give the English meaning. The workbook's example is おおきい, 大きい, big.
  • テスト I: pick the right hiragana reading from four choices.
  • テスト II: pick the right kanji from four choices.

In the tests, the answer is the number of the correct choice, with the choice itself in brackets.

Lesson 4: 半 to 毎 (kanji 31 to 40)

#WordAnswerWhy

#WordAnswerWhy

4せんげつ2 (先月)Last month is 先月. 今月 is this month and 来月 is next month.
5きょう4 (今日)Today is 今日.
6さきに1 (先)先 is ahead. 生 is life, 半 is half and 来 is come.
7よねんかん4 (四年間)間 is 日 inside the gate. 門, 聞 and 問 are look-alikes.
8いま1 (今)Now is 今. 本, 人 and 女 are other kanji.
9ことし4 (今年)This year is 今年. 来年 is next year.
10まいしゅう2 (毎週)Every week is 毎週. 毎日 is every day, 毎月 is every month and 毎年 is every year.

#WordAnswerWhy
1じょうず1 (上手)Good at is 上手. 下手 is poor at (へた).
2した4 (下)Below is 下. 上 is up.
3みぎ2 (右)Right is 右. 石 (stone) is a look-alike.
4きた1 (北)North is 北.
5なか3 (中)Inside is 中.
6ひがし3 (東)East is 東, the sun inside a tree.
7ひだり4 (左)Left is 左. 右 is right.
8そと4 (外)Outside is 外. 夕, 多 and ト are look-alikes made from its parts.

items.b: Sound rules that trip people up
items.h: 1. Small tsu (っ ッ) doubles the next consonant. You hold a tiny pause before it. がっこう is gak-kou (school), きっぷ is kip-pu (ticket) and きって is kit-te (postal stamp). In katakana, ベッド is bed-do (bed) and カップ is kap-pu (cup).

items.h: The Kanji Workbook N5 teaches kanji 1 to 30 in three lessons: the numbers 1 to 10, then bigger numbers with the days of the week, then people and money. The answers to the workbook's own exercises are in the separate answer key.

items.h: Every verb has a formal form that ends in ます, and a dictionary form. items.b: Easy to mix up

items.b: Easy to mix up › Markers that look alike
cells: へ / に (heading to) vs に (exact time)
After a place, へ or に means to. After a time word, に means at or on.
うみへ いきます (I go to the sea) vs 九時に いきます (I go at nine)

items.b: Easy to mix up › Markers that look alike
cells: へ vs で with a place
Going to a place takes へ or に. Doing something at a place takes で.
うみへ いきます (I go to the sea) vs うみで およぎます (I swim in the sea)

items.h: Two big ideas run through this chapter. First, a noun that names an action can become a verb just by adding する. Second, the polite ます forms from Chapter 7 have casual twins, called the plain forms, and those are what friends and family actually say. The last two patterns, の and わ, are sentence endings that give casual speech its flavor.

items.b: Grammar: the patterns Chapter 10 teaches, with examples › 10.1 Noun + する (します)
items.h: A noun verb is built by adding する to a noun that names an action. べんきょう (study) + する = べんきょうする, to study. Only the する part changes, so the whole verb follows する in every form: します, しません, しました, しませんでした in polite speech, and しない, した, しなかった in plain speech. Sports work the same way: テニス + する means play tennis. You will also see を in front of する, as in ゲームを する (play a game).
